The spell weaver however, named Ordaana, lost the control over herself after the mage queen rejected her, and burned down her own glade. Luckily, Thuralin and the child could flee.

Like his horseman, Edrael is a legendary rider. His skills are well known, even outside the realm yet other kin mostly try to avoid being with him. The daily confrontation with invaders in the wood, made him incredibly suspicious and prejudging… even against elves of other high realms.

Valarion counts as one of the best riders of the Skymark Reaches. He is a skilled archer and rider at the same time and leads a warband of glade riders under his banner. He and his lord Edrael usually compete in horse races and hunting duels, competing for being the best rider of glades.

Together with her Wildwood rangers, Lady Draya’s concern is mostly the defense from the evil tree spirits. It is no wonder she doesn’t like to talk a lot, especially to outsiders and even other forest spirits. For her, it often feels absurd how other Asrai fail to understand the other side of the forest spirits. Nevertheless her integrity to the rest of Атэль Лорэн is not harmed by her daily business.

Zeylin is one of the best Wildwood rangers Draya ever served. She trusts him enough that he is leading a Kitband of Wildwood rangers. While he is less reserved and sometimes even quite talkative, he shares the very same worries as her Lady.

Lady Heggria is on par with her wardancer’s skills. Her coldblooded-ness and calculating manner however, allows her to lead the High realm, and control the focus of her dancers. She might therefore not be the most impressive dancer that seeks the ultimate challenge in combat, but she makes sure that all her dancers will find it and get a chance to demonstrate their abilities.

Wychwethyl gained his title from the outstanding agility, quickness, and savagery during combat. He is one of the most exceptional Wardancers of Атэль Лорэн. Every spring, Wychwethyl performs the ritual dance, for a new reign period of the King and Queen of Атэль Лорэн.

Untypical for the most wood elves, for Arias, there is only hate and envy and hunger for power. Why should his realm be the only one that did not recover from Ariel's phase of spreading corruption? A question he often asks himself in the silence of his dark throne room. For him, the other High realms are either too weak and cowardly to help him maintain control over the mid night glade, or they plan to fall on his back the moment he shows a sign of weakness. For both reasons, the Lord is isolating him more and more from the discussions of the Elven Courts.

Morlanna spends most of her time studying Dhar, the Dark magic. She is probably the best Dark weaver on this side of the Ocean, on par with the Asrai’s cousins of Naggaroth. Her interest in the Dark side of Атэль Лорэн, has ever grown.

Lady Arda patrols pathways of the many moonstones of the high realm. While the harmony is rarely disturbed, whoever dares to do so will face death. In her rows every single guardian is learning from their beginning of their service, to protect the living, and respect the dead. After each battle, even outside her realm, fallen troops are respected with all honors after each and every fought battle, while a moon stone is prepared in their halls.

Naneith knows the art of divination, a very rare and secret lore used upon the Asrai Spell weaver. Her power allows her to predict immediate dangers and sense the flow of magic deep in the ground of Атэль Лорэн. She became so proficient in interpreting the signals of the future, that she is known among the Asrai as the Prophetess.

The legendary smith of the forges of Торгаван is blind yet, his work is the most outstanding craftsmanship any elf could see.It is said that Daith is the oldest elf ever existing. People date his works back to the creation of Armour of Aenarion of the first Phoenix King. With that, he is probably even older than Ariel and Orion. Neither his blindness, nor his age seem to affect his performance.

Calanoth made himself a name as one of the deadliest Warriors in the Forest of Loren. Originally, he was a wizard apprentice, who could make use of his talents when he and his master were ambushed by an orc warband. A few of his arrows are decorated with rubies which he only uses for his most worthy foes. It is said that he is still a magician, his powers just manifested in his bow.

Lord Findol is known to be a Masterful Ambusher. He is feared and admired for his tactical superiority inside the Asrai territory. Noteworthy, his attack on a dwarven treasure expedition of Grungi Goldfinger, left him with more foes than friends outside the woods. However, everyone who tries to trespass the woods, for his head or the treasures of Атэль Лорэн, will knows that they could be seconds away from another ambush of the legendary Glade Lord.

While her husband is keeping invading forces away, Evelyne is ruling and organizing the realm of Відрыёт. As Devastating the Ambushes of her husband are, they require a lot of organization, coordination, and maintenance for hidden pathways. A circumstance, her husband often neglects, and even more important, that she is keeping her husband's back.
Not as Fiery as her sister, Arahan is acting considerate, and prefers the dispute over combat. Nevertheless allows her rational stance to analyze and conclude the right tactical decisions in combat.

In contrast to her sister, Naestra is often said to embody the Dark nature of Ariel. She is impatient, impulsive and devious, and knows when it’s the best time to switch to the offensive, be in the dialogue, or hunt her enemies down.

Queen Marrsith is the fourth regent in Laurelorns 4000 year history. Her Great grandmother, Marvel, was Handmaiden to Ulthuan’s Everqueen when she was chosen by the High Council to become the Лаўрэлорн’s first queen during the War of the Beard. Maruviel was the daughter of Aenarion’s first son Morelion, making Queen Marrisith a descendant of the first Phoenix King. Despite having ruled the Лаўрэлорн for centuries, the queen is very much still young for elvish royal standards, having her delegate most of her authority to the much older High Council. Queen Marrsith also has the power of seeing the future, with Queen marrsith seeming to keep secrets of the portents she has experienced.

Prince Aesryn is one who is steeped in jealousy over his Sister. To him, being the Queen (Or King) of Лаўрэлорн should be a great responsibility. But from what Aesryn is seeing, that responsibility is delegated to the High Council, making Marrsith’s position more of a waste than anything. His jealousy set aside, Aesryn also wants to restore the Dragon Tower, an ancient remnant of the Elves, before the war of the beards. This time however, the tower would be cleansed from the arrogance of the Asur.

Yadoh served Queen Marrisith for over 4000 years and is her oldest Champion. As her first champion in her rows, he experienced all troubles Лаўрэлорн and the Eonir, from the Sundering, over the War of the Beards until the recent struggles against the chaos. In all these times, he was a loyal servant of his queen.

The Kithbands of Galenstra guard the marshes of the Ward of the Rain since before the War of the Beards. His keen attitude and excellent knowledge of the terrain makes it almost impossible for the disorganized warbands of the beastmen or any other threat lurking in the south of Лаўрэлорн to enter the forest.

Elora father served as Lionguard of the Pheonix King As first offspring in the Лаўрэлорн forest and finalizing the initial ritus, she is the first generation of her family being perceived as a Faniour, the forest born kindred of the Eonir. She learned from her father the traditions, the combat, and why there is no place for Asurian arrogance in the struggle for survival.

Garelion is one of the patrol Captains protecting the southern part of the Лаўрэлорн forest. Is quite a talkative individual when he is met on a campfire. He likes to visit a human tavern from now and then and is quite popular among the people. This changes quickly when he is sent on patrol missions in the swamps. Meeting him here could be your first and last encounter with him.

Kaia is a powerful Spellcaster using her powers to oversee the Sea of Claws up the coast of Albion. Inhabitants of Nordlands and Norsemen gave her the infamous name Stormwitch which she accepts now as her own. She is calculating as she is beautiful. She takes her decision opportune. So it is not surprising she signed trading agreements with the druchis and rather sought peaceful interactions with norsemen. However whenever somebody tries to trick her they will understand why she is called the Storm witch.

The Family of the Tide Striders, reach far back to northern Ulthuan province Cotique, which held thriving trade relations with the Asur colony which became Лаўрэлорн. During the war of the beards, whenever the time allowed, Lord Adon went up the tower Se-Anthil, watched the shore and desperately watched out for the fleet of the Asur. However, their help never came, and everyday, he lost more hope in the Asur until a point he realizes that the Eonir better form their own kingdom. Today he smiles upon his naivety. He admires Kaia’s keenness, and sees no problem in the diplomatic exchange and trade with the Druchii.

Flyson is usually occupied with many diplomatic missions around the world spending more time on foreign embassies and Courts of Asrai and Druchii, that he often is perceived as foreign and soft from the most of his kin. While indeed he has a weakness for good wine and the elegance of the world's courts, it is his silver tongue that resolved diplomatic issues and saved the existence of his people - which everyone appreciates.

Altarion once was one of the most powerful archmages of Ulthuan. He was since the very beginning of his career interested in the nature of Dragons and how to tame them. Together with other Archmages of Caledor, he once tried to bind the creatures to their will, using the so-called ‘Fell Fangs’. This was perceived as an act of treason which led to him being expelled from the Asurian community and exiled to Лаўрэлорн forest. Like many other of the expelled ‘Greylords’, he built himself a residence somewhere in the Silverwood, where he continued his experiments. When Altharion is not busy with his studies, he somewhat grows an interest in keeping pesking forces away from his laboratories, which let him help the Warden of the Sun from time to time. Which makes him an unusual and selfish - but also powerful ally of the Eonir.

While Lindialoc is keeping strong trade ties with the Government of Salzenmünd, he is also the one putting tensions into these relations. He disobeys direct decisions originating from the High Council just to achieve additional concessions that benefit the elves. While he certainly does not win supporters in the High Council, the elves do admire his cunning to achieve Лаўрэлорн’s Interest in the Empire of Men.

There are secrets in Лаўрэлорн, which seldomly belong in nobody else's hands than those who owe to protect them.The hermit Athanoc is tired of his burden. Yet he doesn’t anybody to gain knowledge about the magic of athel loren.

Iyana is leading a Kithband of Eonir Warriors, defending her homeland against the Norse invaders. While she is disillusioned that laurelorn ever shines as it did centuries ago, she is practical, inventive, and adapts to the situation her people are living in. She has good relations with human locals around the Wardens and rather appreciates their support, than seeing them as invaders of Лаўрэлорн.

Ungrim Ironfist is the Slayer King of Карак-Кадрын. There has never before been a Dwarf more torn between his duties than Ungrim Ironfist. As the King of Карак-Кадрын, he is oathbound to protect his kingdom and his people. As the patriarch of the Ангрулок Clan, he has to ensure that his relatives succeed, and as a sworn Slayer who has taken the oath, Ungrim is also bound to seek his doom against the most powerful foe he can find. Never content to sit back on his throne and wait, Ungrim looks for any opportunity to lead his throngs to war. There are few kinds of monsters that walk the world that Ungrim Ironfist has not slain in battle. Armed with the enormous Axe of Dargo, Ungrim deals death, carving a path of red ruin before him while singing songs of old in a booming voice. Atop his head is a bright orange crest that rises above a sturdy horned helmet set with a golden crown. For Ungrim is both a Slayer and a King, more than likely the last of the line of Slayer Kings of Карак-Кадрын.

Dorin Flamebeard is a living embodiment of vengeance, his fiery orange beard streaked with soot and ash as if reflecting the blazing inferno of his wrath. Once a proud warrior of Карак-Кадрын, Dorin swore the Slayer Oath after failing to save his kin from a devastating Greenskin raid that left an entire mining outpost in ruins. Now, he roams the battlefields seeking redemption in death, though none have yet been able to grant him the release he craves. Dorin wields a giant greataxe, its edge glowing faintly red as if kissed by the forge. His bare chest is a canvas of scars, each one a testament to battles fought against trolls, wyverns, and even a dreaded Chimera. Dorin’s ferocity in combat is unmatched, his movements a whirlwind of strikes that leave foes in pieces before they can react. His fiery demeanour matches his appearance; he is quick to anger but equally quick to inspire those who fight alongside him. Among the Slayers of Карак-Кадрын, Dorin is revered as a hero, even if he rejects such accolades. For him, every battle is a step closer to the redemption he seeks but has yet to find.

Ulfar Stonebane is a towering figure among the Slayers of Карак-Кадрын, his immense frame and booming voice making him a presence that cannot be ignored. Before taking the Slayer Oath, Ulfar was a miner of great renown, known for his ability to carve through solid stone with unparalleled speed and precision. His path to dishonour came when he led his mining crew into a cavern infested with Skaven, resulting in the loss of many lives, including his younger brother. Wracked with guilt, he swore to seek a glorious death in battle. Ulfar wields a massive two-handed war axe, its edge engraved with runes of destruction that amplify the force of his strikes. His fighting style is as relentless as an avalanche, crushing everything in his path with devastating swings. His sheer physical power allows him to go toe-to-toe with some of the largest foes, from Chaos Trolls to the towering beasts of the Ogre Kingdoms. Despite his grim purpose, Ulfar has a deep, booming laugh that echoes through the halls of Карак-Кадрын, and he often shares tales of his battles over tankards of ale.

Skaldi Doomshard is a grim and brooding figure, his face half-covered in burn scars from a failed attempt to slay a Hellcannon of Chaos that had laid waste to a Dwarf outpost. Though he succeeded in destroying the infernal war machine, the magical backlash from its destruction left him disfigured and filled with a deep-seated hatred for the forces of Chaos. From that day forward, Skaldi has dedicated his life to hunting daemons and their mortal servants, his every strike fuelled by a burning desire for vengeance. Skaldi’s weapon of choice is a great axe, its blade etched with ancient runes of warding and banishment. The weapon is said to hum faintly in the presence of Chaos, guiding Skaldi’s strikes with uncanny precision. Unlike many Slayers, Skaldi is not prone to boisterousness or revelry. He is a solitary figure, often seen sharpening his axe or muttering ancient oaths under his breath. His dour demeanour and single-minded focus on his task make him an intimidating presence, even among his fellow Slayers. Despite this, Skaldi is respected for his unyielding determination and his ability to face even the most horrific foes without flinching. Among the halls of Карак-Кадрын, his name is whispered with a mixture of awe and sorrow, for Skaldi Doomshard is a Slayer whose path is paved with fire and blood.

In the halls of Карак-Кадрын, where the echoes of oaths and battle cries fill the air, one Dwarf stands apart, not as a Slayer, but as their guide and keeper of the ancient arts. Runelord Thori Runescorch is no outcast, nor does he seek the glorious death the Slayers crave, yet he walks among them as a mentor, a smith, and a force that pushes them beyond their limits. Clad in thick gromril armour etched with radiant runes of fire and might, Thori embodies the fury of the forge, a flame that drives the Slayers ever forward. Unlike many of his kin, Thori does not scorn the Slayers for their choice. Instead, he sees them as Dwarfs who have embraced the most dangerous path a son of Grungni can take. It is his duty, then, to ensure that when they march to battle, they do so wielding weapons and blessings worthy of their sacrifice. From his forge beneath Карак-Кадрын’s great hall, he inscribes burning runes onto axes, hammers, and even the flesh of willing Slayers, igniting their wrath to new heights. His 'Runes of the Forgeheart' sear into their weapons, making them burn like the heart of a volcano, while his 'Runes of the Phoenix' infuse the Slayers with an unyielding fire that keeps them fighting even through wounds that would fell lesser warriors.Thori himself is no mere smith, nor does he hide in the safety of the hold. In battle, he wields a rune-etched hammer that leaves trails of fire in its wake, each strike bursting into flames that sear foes to cinders. He stands at the threshold between the living and the dead, ensuring that no Slayer’s sacrifice is in vain. Though he does not seek his own doom, he will not shirk from battle, and should his death come, he knows it will be in service to his kin.

In the annals of Карак-Кадрын, few Slayers have carved a path of destruction as fearsome as Hengist Doomcleaver. A grim and towering figure, his body is a patchwork of scars, each wound a testament to a battle fought and a foe slain. His once-golden beard is now streaked with crimson from the endless slaughter, and his piercing gaze burns with the embers of vengeance. Hengist has hunted daemons for decades, cleaving through their twisted forms with his Greataxe, inscribed with runes of banishment that sever the unnatural ties that bind them to the mortal realm. Hengist does not revel in battle like some of his Slayer kin; he treats it as a duty, a debt to be repaid in blood for some long-forgotten disgrace. He does not boast, nor does he drink in the halls of Карак-Кадрын, for his oath consumes him utterly. When daemons pour forth from rifts or corrupted lands, it is Hengist who leads the charge, cutting them down like a reaper at harvest. To see him in battle is to witness a storm of steel and blood, his axe flashing in great arcs, each swing driving back the tide of the unnatural. Though he seeks his end, fate has denied him time and again. He has faced greater daemons and survived, his hatred burning ever fiercer. The Doomcleaver walks a path from which there is no return, and until he falls, he will continue carving his name into the annals of Карак-Кадрын in the blood of the damned.

Rurik Earthshaker was once a king’s champion, a warrior of unmatched skill who stood beside Карак-Кадрын’s rulers in times of war. But betrayal and failure tainted his honour, and so he cast aside his title, his riches, and his pride, swearing himself to the Slayer’s Oath. From that day forth, he became a slayer who sought out only the most fearsome and monstrous foes to earn his redemption Unlike many Slayers who fight alone, Rurik leads bands of his kin into battle, carving through the horrors of the world in a whirlwind of blood and fire. His weapon is a mighty great axe inscribed with runes of ruin, and its edge burns with white-hot fury when turned against the creatures of Chaos. He has hunted across the Worlds Edge Mountains and beyond, facing greater daemons, mutated dragonspawn, and creatures of nightmare that few would dare name aloud.

Among the Slayers of Карак-Кадрын, Urist Ironbane is a legend whispered in awe and dread alike. His very name is a curse upon the dark forces of Chaos, for no daemon, beast, or monster has yet managed to lay him low. It is not for lack of trying, Urist has hurled himself into battles that should have claimed his life a hundred times over. Yet each time, he emerges, bloodied but unbowed, his mighty Waraxe still swinging with undiminished wrath. Urist’s path to the Slayer cult was paved in sorrow and ruin. Once the lord of a great hold now lost to the tides of Chaos, he swore his oath after witnessing his kin slaughtered, his halls desecrated, and his legacy reduced to nothing. But his death did not come as he had hoped. Every battle he fought should have claimed him, yet fate seemed to mock his suffering, keeping him alive even against overwhelming odds. He has faced daemons of Khorne in single combat, endured the warpfire of Tzeentch’s horrors, and stood against a Verminlord with nothing but his bare hands, and still he lives. Many whisper that Urist is cursed, that his doom will never come, and that he is fated to wander the earth as a Slayer who will never die. Whatever the truth, the Undying Slayer fights on, his hatred undimmed, his wrath eternal. Perhaps one day, he will meet his end at the hands of a foe truly worthy of his fury, but until that day, the enemies of the Dawi will tremble before his name.

Once among the most respected thanes of Карак-Кадрын, Bolli Vorgrun stood as the unyielding rock upon which countless enemy assaults were shattered. A warrior of indomitable spirit and steadfast discipline, Bolli spent decades defending the Slayer Keep’s outer fortifications, holding the walls against the greenskin hordes, Chaos warbands, and the monstrosities that threatened the ancestral home of Grimnir’s chosen. He was a shield-brother to kings, a hammer that never faltered, and a voice of wisdom in the feasting halls. But even the strongest stones can crack. In the last great siege of Карак-Кадрын, Bolli led a vanguard force to break the lines of a Chaos incursion led by a monstrous warlord. The battle raged for days, and though Bolli and his warriors fought with unrelenting fury, their position was overrun. He was left for dead amid the bodies of his slain comrades, the sight of his warriors being torn apart forever etched into his memory. When he awoke, he was among the survivors, those who had failed to hold the line. The shame was too great to bear. He cast aside his rank and his duties, swearing the Slayer's Oath in silent fury. But fate had other plans. King Ungrim Ironfist himself intervened, declaring that Bolli was not meant to walk the Slayer’s path, but that of a warrior-lord, one who would bring ruin to the foes of the Dawi with the rage of a Slayer and the discipline of a Thane. And so, Bolli fights on, clad in his rune-inscribed gromril armour, bearing his mighty shield which has turned aside blows from daemon lords and dragonfire alike. No longer a Thane, but something more, a living bastion of Карак-Кадрын, sworn to defend his hold until the very mountains crumble.

The tunnels and mines beneath Карак-Кадрын stretch deeper than most dare to tread, and in those dark, winding passages, one name carries the weight of legend, Dori Magrest. A miner-lord of unmatched skill, he has spent his life in the depths of the earth, carving through stone to uncover hidden riches, lost vaults, and long-forgotten paths. Where others see rock and ruin, Dori sees the veins of the mountain, knowing where to dig and when to hold. Born into a long line of miners, Dori’s name was spoken in reverence even before he took up lordship. His hammer is no mere tool of labour but a rune-etched relic that has struck down both stone and enemy alike. He led countless expeditions into the underways, unearthing lost Dawi relics and recovering the wealth of Карак-Кадрын’s ancestors. Yet, it was his battle against the Skaven of Clan Mors that cemented his place in history. When a massive tunnel collapse left his mining party trapped, he led them in a desperate defence, fending off hordes of chittering vermin in the pitch-black darkness. With naught but pickaxes and sheer determination, Dori and his kin fought their way to the surface, dragging Skaven corpses behind them as proof of their defiance. Now, as a lord of Карак-Кадрын, Dori commands the mountain’s depths, ensuring its wealth remains untapped by the enemy. He has reforged ancient passageways, strengthened collapsed tunnels, and even uncovered long-lost chambers of runic knowledge. But he is no mere overseer, when the time for battle comes, Dori wields his hammer with the same force he would strike a stubborn ore vein, shattering skulls with the might of the mountain itself.

Dorin Silverfoot, son of Haakon Hargrimsson, is a noble Dwarf lord of ancient lineage, descended from the once-proud hold of Karaz Bryn, now lost to the Pale Lady’s cursed dominion. Born amidst exile and raised among the dispossessed. As a young warrior, Dorin’s life was torn apart when a Greenskin warband descended upon his encampment. His entire family was slaughtered, yet by some miracle, or the will of the Ancestor gods, Dorin survived, found unconscious in the remains of a bloodied tent, surrounded by the mangled corpses of Orcs and Goblins. While he lingered on the edge of death, the priests who looked over the dead discerned something unusual in the lad. Upon consulting the ancient genealogies and rune-stones, they uncovered a truth long buried: Dorin was of royal blood, a direct descendant of Razek Silverfoot, Thane of Karaz Bryn and son of King Borri Silverfoot. When Dorin awoke, he found the healers, warriors, and even the priests bowing before him. From that day forward, his destiny changed. Trained by the finest warriors among the dispossessed clans, Dorin proved a gifted and determined pupil, rising swiftly through their ranks until he bested his own master in single combat. With axe and shield, he earned not only respect but also loyalty. Now recognised as a lord and leader, Dorin Haakonsson leads daring raids into the blighted lands near Karak Ungor and Karaz Bryn, harassing enemy patrols, reclaiming long-lost mines, and reforging the pride of his fallen people. Though cautious and calculating, Dorin bears a simmering resolve; he knows the time draws near when the Dawi shall march to reclaim Karak Ungor. And after that, his path will lead to Karaz Bryn itself and the reckoning that awaits within its cursed halls.

Furgil Emberkeeper is the last surviving Runelord of Karaz Bryn, the once-proud hold now lost to shadow and undeath. A master of ancient lore and sacred craft, Furgil earned his name during the doomed final days of the hold, when he gathered the most precious relics of his people, the sacred rune-scrolls, oath-stones, and a shard of the hold's Eternal Forge-fire, and led a desperate retreat through crumbling halls and bloodied tunnels. Many fell in the retreat, runesmiths torn apart by rampaging Greenskins, others dragged screaming into the dark by the Pale Queen’s cursed minions, but Furgil endured. Scarred, wearied, and burdened by loss, he now leads a cadre of loyal runesmiths in exile, teaching them the forgotten rune-lore of Karaz Bryn and fuelling in them the fire of vengeance. Though older than stone and grimmer than iron, Furgil’s skill at the forge has not waned. Each weapon he crafts is a masterpiece of wrath and remembrance: blades etched with runes to keep the dead from rising, warhammers that strike with the fury of the ancestors, and blessed axes to cleave through troll-hide in a single blow. These are no mere tools of war; they are heirlooms of a grudge not yet settled. Furgil has sworn a mighty oath: he shall not pass into the halls of his forebears until Karaz Bryn is reclaimed and the Pale Queen burns in its forge like the cursed abomination she is. It is for this reason, with a heavy heart and reluctant hand, that Furgil now lends his knowledge to weaken the corrupted rune-wards that still bolster Karak Ungor’s walls. He does so not for glory, but because he sees no other path forward. The sooner Karak Ungor falls, the sooner the great reckoning can begin, and Furgil Emberkeeper will be there to see it done.

Kazgar Bonecleaver was once a proud warrior of Karaz Bryn, until the cursed day the hold fell to the Pale Lady and her undead host. In the choking darkness of a desecrated shrine deep beneath the earth, Kazgar was forced to watch as his wife and children were sacrificed upon a foreign, rune-scarred altar. He would have struck then and there, roaring with grief and fury, but fate had other plans. A Dwarfen rescue party dragged him away screaming, while the Pale Lady's cruel laughter echoed through the caverns like a taunt from some forgotten nightmare. Broken in spirit and consumed by wrath, Kazgar refused to rejoin his surviving kin. Instead, he made the long and bitter trek to Карак-Кадрын, where he took the Slayer's Oath before the ancestors. No longer a warrior of a hold but a seeker of a glorious death, Kazgar wandered far and wide, westward to battle the shambling horrors of the dead and northward to clash with the daemons and beasts of Chaos. Yet no foe, no wound, no fury could grant him the release he sought. He did not die. And in every fitful sleep, the Pale Lady’s laughter haunted him still. Now, Kazgar has returned, his mind fraying like an old banner in the wind, his body a patchwork of scars and half-healed wounds. Reunited with the remnants of his kin, he has decided to use their lands as a base of operations. From their redoubts, he launches relentless raids into the cursed depths of Karaz Bryn, seeking one thing and one thing only: to silence the laughter.

Vragni is as old as the mountains are grey and among the last living Dwarfs who still remember the fall of Karak Ungor. He was there when the hold's garrison made its final, desperate stand against the greenskin tide from below. Though the warriors fought with grim valour, with their backs against the walls and without the main host of Karak Ungor to reinforce them, they could not stem the horde. Knowing the hold was lost, Vragni sounded the retreat, guiding the survivors out the gates and into the southern reaches of Карак-Кадрын. King Morek Stonehammer never forgave him for this outrage. When the old king perished, Vragni became an advisor to the scattered lords and stewards of the displaced clans. But as the years ground on, his words grew fewer, and his counsel was less sought. Whether from grief, shame, or the slow wear of time, Vragni's voice faded from the halls of leadership. Now, Vragni lives only to fight and drink, burying the old pain in battle and ale. On the field, he is a masterful commander, silent, watchful, and possessed of a battlefield instinct bordering on the supernatural. His warriors move with uncanny precision, often taking up complex formations at the utterance of a single gruff word. In silence, Vragni has found his purpose once more.

Thori Shattershield is a battle-hardened lord of Karak Ungor, born and raised in exile among the scattered remnants of his fallen hold. Though denied the stone halls of his ancestors, Thori was forged in the hardship and bitterness of the wilderness, his resolve tempered by the unrelenting struggle for survival against greenskins, undead, and worse. His name was earned during a brutal ambush upon a caravan of exiled clans. In the heart of the melee, Thori came face-to-face with a hulking Orc warboss. The two clashed in single combat, and though Thori was eventually disarmed, he refused to yield. With a roar, he shattered his heavy oaken shield against the beast’s skull, caving it in and felling the brute where it stood. The remaining Orcs, leaderless and stunned, broke and fled into the hills. Since that day, the name Shattershield has been spoken with respect among the exiles of Karak Ungor. Thori has become a symbol of their enduring defiance, leading raids into the lost hold’s outer tunnels and vowing that the day of reckoning will come when the kin of Karak Ungor march once more beneath the mountain.

Haming the Rock, once mockingly known as Haming the Wazzok, is a Dwarf lord of Karaz Bryn, renowned not for wit or wisdom, but for indomitable strength and unshakable resolve. Taller and broader than most of his kin, Haming's intellect is not his strongest asset, a fact he acknowledges without shame. He wisely entrusts the finer details of command and drill to his more sharp-minded subordinates. Tasked with the grim duty of reclaiming an old mine infested by the undead, one the Pale Lady had attempted to retake using her minions, Haming led a force to both cleanse the tunnels and rescue any surviving miners still trapped within. During the assault, Haming was separated from his warband while battling a towering undead giant. As he fought his way through the gloom, he came upon a narrow chamber where a group of young miners had been cornered against a wall, a shambling horde of skeletal and rotting horrors closing in. Without hesitation, Haming threw himself into the breach, wedging his massive bulk between the undead and his kin. He held the narrow corridor alone, a wall of iron and fury, enduring blow after blow as the miners slipped past him to safety. Rotten clubs and rusted blades alike broke against his armour, but he would not fall. Not while a single Dwarf remained in danger. When his unit finally caught up with him, they found Haming battered, bloodied, and breathing heavily, yet still standing. The dead lay in heaps at his feet. He said nothing, but the cheers and laughter of his kin told him all he needed to know. From that day forth, none have dared call him a Wazzok. Now he is Haming the Rock, the immovable shield of Karaz Bryn, and he swears that all who threaten his kin shall be ground to gristle beneath his boots.

Norgrim the Lost is a grim and haunted lord of Karak Ungor, known amongst the clans as much for his uncanny survival as for the mystery that shrouds his past. Once thought slain during the fall of Karak Ungor, Norgrim vanished beneath the mountain as the greenskins poured through its tunnels. For decades, no word of him reached the exiled clans, until he emerged, gaunt and battle-worn, bearing scars both seen and unseen. None know precisely where Norgrim spent those long years. Some whisper he wandered the deepest holds alone, hunting the greenskins that defiled his ancestral home. Others claim he walked the winding, cursed tunnels of the World’s Edge beneath the notice of gods or daemons. A few even say he died, and that what returned is not quite Dwarf. What is known is this: Norgrim returned changed. His eyes burn with a quiet fury, and his voice carries the weight of ancient grief. He speaks little of what he endured, save to mutter darkly of the 'echoing silence' and the 'things that dwell where even the Thaggoraki will not.' He bears an heirloom axe, once thought lost with Karak Ungor, and a tattered banner which he refuses to let any other Dwarf touch. Norgrim has become a rallying figure for those who dream of reclaiming the lost hold. He leads sorties with cold precision and relentless purpose, striking at goblin encampments and cursed crypts alike, ever drawing closer to the gates of Karak Ungor. To his foes, he is a vengeful shadow from the deep. To his kin, he is a symbol of endurance and vengeance, the Dwarf who was lost, and who will stop at nothing to see his home reclaimed.

Mendri Blackpowder is an eccentric and sharp-witted Engineer of Karak Ungor descent, born and raised in exile amidst the scattered remnants of the lost hold’s clans. Charged with the fabrication and upkeep of siege engines and blackpowder weaponry, Mendri serves as a vital cog in the efforts to sustain and advance the military might of the displaced Dwarfs of Karak Ungor and Karaz Bryn. In the long years of exile, resources have been scarce and machinery scarcer still. Mendri and his fellow Engineers have been forced to innovate, repair, and repurpose old weaponry with dwindling supplies, always struggling to keep the forges burning and the guns firing. Yet, in Mendri’s inventive mind, frustration breeds ambition, and ambition, in turn, has birthed a radical solution. Where others see the unbreachable walls and impenetrable gates of Karak Ungor, Mendri sees a flaw to be exploited. He argues, with wild gesticulations and blackpowder-laced breath, that the hold cannot be retaken by conventional means. Decades of failed assaults prove as much. His proposal? Blow it up. Explosives placed in key locations in the hold, the walls and the tunnels would collapse a large part of the city, bury its enemies beneath it, and leave nothing for the greenskins to crawl back to. In his mind this would kill a large part of the greenskins and force the rest to retreat underground, with the tunnels collapsing behind them, allowing the Dwarfs to march right in from the surface. The lords and Thanes scoffed, of course. Some called him mad. Others, worse. But as the years drag on, more have begun to wonder, in hushed tones and dark chambers, whether madness might not, in fact, be genius. Mendri Blackpowder waits, blueprint in hand and powder dry, for the day his plan is given its chance. And when that day comes, the earth shall tremble.

Duregar, King of Карак-Ангазхар and patriarch of Clan Бранмаказ, has long stood as a stalwart protector of Black Fire Pass. For many decades, he commanded the defences that held the mountain pass against countless incursions. In more recent years, however, he has passed this responsibility to his son, Baragor, entrusting him with the fortress’s continued vigilance. Now focused primarily on overseeing the hold’s trade and the management of its wealth, Duregar nonetheless remains a warrior-king at heart. He frequently leads sorties into the surrounding regions, seeking to settle grudges recorded in the Angazhar Kron. His hatred for the Grobi runs particularly deep; ever since a cunning raid saw a tribe of Night Goblins plunder one of Карак-Ангазхар’s obsidian mines, he has harboured a personal vendetta against their kind. Their use of cowardly trickery to abscond with cartloads of precious obsidian remains a black mark in the king’s memory, and one he swears to avenge in full.

Baragor has proven his mettle time and again, earning the respect of warriors and Thanes alike. Yet despite the fame of Карак-Ангазхар’s obsidian axes, he steadfastly refuses to wield one. Instead, he places his trust in the oldest allies of the Dwarfs, iron and steel. It was iron and steel that defended Black Fire Pass for centuries, and in Baragor’s eyes, it shall be iron and steel that continue to do so. A staunch traditionalist, Baragor views many of the Engineers’ Guild’s more recent innovations with open scepticism. Guns, he admits, have their place, but what good are black powder and gearwork when the true glory lies in hearing a thrice-blessed suit of armour ring out as an Urki blade shatters upon it? To Baragor, the Dawi’s strength lies not in inventions, but in honour, endurance, and cold-forged steel.

Harek Grimbeard is a revered Longbeard of Карак-Ангазхар, his name etched with honour in the hold’s records following the infamous Battle of the Gap. During that dark hour, a violent collapse within the Underway tunnels severed Harek from his unit. Trapped behind the rubble with naught but a handful of miners, he found himself standing alone against the skittering tide of goblins that poured forth from the darkness. A narrow gap between two mounds of stone was all that separated the beleaguered miners from the enemy. Harek planted himself in that breach like an iron-banded wall, shield high and axe flashing in the gloom. Goblin blades struck from every angle, clawed hands grasped through the gap, but none made it past the old warrior. Using the confined space to his advantage, Harek held the line with grim determination, felling countless Grobi with each swing. It was only when reinforcements finally broke through the flanks that the goblins were driven back into the shadows. Though wounded and weary, Harek stood tall amidst the carnage, his armour slick with gore and his beard stiff with blood.

When a young clan-dwarf first emerges from the mines and takes up his inaugural az, it is tradition that he does not do so alone. Though the Dwarfs are many things; stubborn, proud, and unyielding, reckless is not one of them. No beardling is sent to war without guidance, for even the stoutest heart must be tempered by experience. That is where Drong Steelpick comes in. Drong commands a company of hardened veterans and wide-eyed beardlings, leading them into their first battles upon the surface. His role is not simply that of a warrior, but a teacher, ensuring that the young Dwarfs learn not just how to swing an axe, but how to survive. Under Drong’s watchful eye, beardlings learn to hold the line, to read an enemy’s movements, and to trust the shield beside them. Stoic and battle-worn, Drong has marched against Beastmen, Greenskins, and worse, always returning with fewer in his ranks but stronger warriors beside him. His presence is both reassuring and immovable, a living bulwark who teaches through example. Many a famed Thane once swung their first axe under Drong’s command.

Alf Thomsson is the current captain of the Ebonshard Brotherhood, an elite fighting force renowned for wielding axes edged with obsidian, mined from the depths beneath Карак-Ангазхар. Though the blades are brittle and difficult to forge, they are razor-sharp and deadly in the hands of seasoned warriors. As captain, Alf oversees all aspects of the Brotherhood’s upkeep: from rigorous training schedules and strict quality control of weaponry, to ensuring that the company sees regular combat. He is also responsible for identifying promising warriors from other units who might one day be deemed worthy of joining the Brotherhood. However, the final decision rests with the king, for admittance into the Ebonshard ranks is not given lightly. The Brotherhood is composed almost entirely of veterans, and younger members are a rarity. Alf himself is the oldest of them all, a grim and respected figure who has cut down countless foes in defence of the hold. Though age weighs on his shoulders, his blows are still as precise and brutal as ever. His voice carries great weight in matters of war, and his presence alone can steady even the most uncertain shield line.

Runelord Garil Stoneforged presides over the ancient forges of Карак-Ангазхар, where the famed obsidian-bladed axes of the hold are crafted. Alongside his squad of master Runesmiths, Garil painstakingly inscribes runes of sharpness upon each weapon, ensuring that they bite through armour and bone with an edge no natural forge could provide. Unlike many of his order who remain within the sanctity of the forge halls, Garil often marches to war alongside a company of the Ebonshard Brotherhood. There, amidst the roar of battle, he observes the potency of his rune-craft firsthand. With every clash of blade and shield, he adjusts and reinforces the runes with grim precision, channelling ancient power through hammer and chant to strengthen the might of Dwarf-forged steel in the very heart of battle.

Sven Whitemane is a respected elder of Карак-Ангазхар, a grim and steadfast Dwarf who lost most of his kin in a brutal Greenskin raid. Stricken with grief and fuelled by righteous fury, he has since dedicated the remainder of his days to the destruction of the enemies of the Karaz Ankor.Though he once stood upon the precipice of taking the Slayer's Oath and seeking an honourable death in battle, Sven chose a different path. Instead, he now leads a company of dispossessed Clans Dwarfs, fellow Dawi who, like him, have suffered great loss. Together, they form a vengeful warband whose purpose is not redemption through death, but the reaping of a grim toll upon those who would threaten Dwarfkind.

Kallon Silverbreaker is a renowned Dwarf Lord of Карак-Ангазхар. A calculating and brooding strategist, Kallon is best known for his mastery of defensive warfare.He stood beside Prince Baragor Sharpblade during the defence of Black Fire Pass, when a vast Greenskin horde sought to force its way through. Reinforcements from the Empire were sparse, Аверлянд’s mad Count failed to recognise the true scale of the threat, dismissing the warnings as Dwarfen exaggeration. Undeterred, Kallon made do with what forces he had, employing tactics seldom seen by either Dwarf or Man. His personal unorthodox strategies turned the tide.The battle was won with minimal loss of Dwarfen or Imperial life, and the Greenskins were driven from the pass.

The brawler-king of Карак-Ангазхар, Logan Hammerfist is as renowned for his iron fists as he is for consuming copious amounts of alcohol, even by Dwarfen standards. A towering figure among his kin, Logan’s brawny frame and scarred, calloused knuckles speak of decades spent in brutal close combat, both on the battlefield and in the tavern. His punch, it is said, lands with the force of a warhammer’s swing, capable of shattering a troll’s skull. He is rarely seen without his ancestral gauntlets, Grimdrengi, forged in the hold’s deepest forges and inscribed with runes to channel and enhance his prodigious strength. Though he is a fearsome warrior, Logan’s true love lies in the camaraderie of the feast hall, where tales of glory flow as freely as the ale. Quick to laugh and quicker to anger, he is a steadfast ally, a fierce champion of his hold, and a deadly foe to any who would threaten Карак-Ангазхар.

Durgin Galazbar is a venerable Dwarf Lord, his name etched into the annals of Карак-Ангазхар with runes of honour and remembrance. Clad in thick Gromril plate, adorned with runes of spell-breaking, his armour is a masterwork of Dwarfen craft, rendering him near-impervious to foul magic and capable of withstanding the crushing blows of giants. Renowned for his unyielding resolve and immovable stance, Durgin has long stood as a bulwark against the Greenskin menace, a living shield between his hold and the darkness. Though his beard is long and grey with age, his strength has not waned, and his wisdom is as keen as the edge of a rune-forged axe.

King Thuringar Orc-Hewer unexpectedly ascended to the throne fifty years ago, following the assassination of both his father and elder brother. Since that grim day, King Thuringar has vowed to bring war to the Greenskins and drive them from the Grey Mountains once and for all. Many tribes have already fallen beneath the steel plated boots of his throngs, yet the task of securing the entire range remains long and arduous. Within the Inner Council, opinion is divided. Some hail the king’s campaign as righteous vengeance, while others question the wisdom of such prolonged warfare against a foe that breeds like vermin and strikes from the shadows.

Ganmar Oakheart is the commander of the Ranger Corps of Карак-Азгараз. He seizes every opportunity to venture beyond the hold, whether on scouting missions or in dealings with the Wood Elves. Most dwarfs regard Ganmar’s fondness for the outside world as highly eccentric, if not outright peculiar. His company is composed almost entirely of rangers, like-minded folk who share his affinity for the wilds and a deep mistrust of civilization beyond stone walls and mountain halls.

Harok, ruling lord of Clan Steelcrag of Карак-Азгараз, is a master of siegecraft, both defensive and offensive. Under his command, numerous greenskin raids have been repelled, only to be answered thrice over by thunderous volleys from the hold’s cannons and grudge-throwers. Harok is renowned for his meticulous planning and unrelenting resolve, forging a reputation among friend and foe alike as an unshakeable bulwark of Dwarfen warfare.

Morek Flintbeard is the ruling lord of Clan Flintbeard of Карак-Азгараз, a clan famed for its mastery of close combat and known across the Grey Mountains as the 'Hammer of Карак-Азгараз'. While Hammerers are traditionally sworn to the king’s personal guard, Clan Flintbeard has earned the rare honour of maintaining its own elite unit of Hammerers, warriors who favour aggressive assaults over the usual defensive formations, often fighting shoulder to shoulder with their lord. Morek himself is a formidable warrior, proficient in a variety of melee weapons, some of which are unfamiliar even to other dwarfs. Yet he remains true to Dwarfen steel, bearing into battle a mighty warhammer of ancient make. He maintains strong ties with the Runesmiths of Clan Thunderstone, and his armour is inscribed with powerful runes of endurance and spell-breaking.

Kazrik Cragtooth is the ruling lord of Clan Cragtooth of Карак-Азгараз, a venerable clan whose lineage traces back to the Dragonback Mountains and the lost hold of Ekrund. Once a high-standing warrior clan, they earned lasting honour by covering the retreat of other Dawi during Ekrund’s fall, an act of grim bravery that cost many lives. Though the hold was lost, the Cragtooths endured, and have since dedicated themselves to vengeance, seizing every opportunity to strike against the hated greenskins and vile Skaven. Kazrik himself is a stoic and unyielding figure, known for his iron resolve and unwavering commitment to the defence of the hold. So long as a Cragtooth draws breath, no more dwarf holds shall fall.

Ketil Ironarm is the ruling lord of Clan Ironarm of Карак-Азгараз, one of the founding clans of the hold. Though steeped in tradition and martial pride, the clan is often the subject of jest among other dwarfs, largely due to their perceived arrogance. Some, with beards safely out of reach, even liken them to High Elves, though never to their faces, of course. Mockery aside, few can deny the strength of Clan Ironarm, known for fielding stalwart ranks of Ironbreakers in battle. Ketil himself, mockingly called Angelgi behind his back, is the most boastful of them all, and has left more than a few taverns in ruin over a slight to his honour. Still, none can call him a braggart without cause. Ketil is ever at the vanguard, letting the enemy break upon him and his kin, his armour drenched in gore and glory alike. Even so, many in the hold wouldn’t mind seeing him taken down a peg, or three.

Durak Irebeard is the ruling lord of Clan Irebeard of Карак-Азгараз, one of the founding clans of the hold. Once a proud and fiery lord, Durak took the Slayer’s oath following a grievous dishonour, though he has never spoken of the event that led him to it. Despite becoming a Slayer, he retains his authority within the clan, a rare but not unheard of situation among the dwarfs of the Karaz Ankor. Durak’s rage is the stuff of legend. His roaring voice echoes through the hold, and his presence in battle is nothing short of terrifying. He hurls himself at the largest and most dangerous foes, seeking a glorious end worthy of song and remembrance. Many of Clan Irebeard have followed in his footsteps, their numbers among the Slayers swelling in recent decades. Though Durak still leads them in battle, it is clear he fights not for power or pride, but to redeem a shame he refuses to name.

Ruling Lord of Clan Grimhelm of Карак-Азгараз, one of the founding clans of the hold. Skalf is a Dwarf whose grim visage is as much a part of his identity as the rune-carved helm he bears into battle. As the Lord of Clan Grimhelm, he upholds the clan’s reputation for stoic resilience and unwavering loyalty to Карак-Азгараз His helm, wrought from darkened gromril and adorned with runes of defiance, is a revered heirloom said to have withstood the crushing blows of giants and the foul sorcery of dark wizards alike.

Proud leader of Clan Falconshield, Kallon’s name is synonymous with mastery of the skies and the unyielding defence of his kin. Clad in gleaming gromril plate, he wields a finely wrought war axe and a rune-etched shield said to have turned aside the blades of Greenskin warlords and the claws of Chaos beasts alike. His shield, known as Skyguard, is a revered heirloom of his clan, forged by the Runesmiths of Карак-Азгараз and imbued with runes of protection and resilience. Though a lord of iron discipline and unshakable resolve, Kallon is also a skilled falconer, and his heart soars with the same freedom as his birds. He is often found in the high crags above the hold, releasing his falcons to wheel and dive in the mountain winds, their cries echoing across the peaks. These birds serve not only as companions but as scouts and messengers for the hold, their keen eyes and swift wings offering early warning of any approaching threat.

The venerable Runelord of Clan Thunder-Stone stands as a living testament to the enduring might and craftsmanship of the Dwarfs of Карак-Азгараз. With a beard as white as mountain snow, braided with rune-inscribed bands, Grundi’s visage is one of ancient wisdom and unyielding resolve. His rune-etched armour gleams faintly with the light of protective wards, each rune inscribed with the meticulous precision born of centuries of practice. He bears the ancestral weapon of his clan, a mighty warhammer whose head is hewn from enchanted granite and crackles with runic energy that echoes the fury of a lightning storm. When wielded in battle, it strikes with the force of an avalanche, casting enemies aside like leaves upon the wind. To stand against Grundi Thunder-Stone is to face the wrath of the mountains themselves, a fury that no foe, however formidable, has yet endured and lived to tell of it.

The venerable king of Карак-Экcьфілаз and ruler of clan steelclad. His gromril armour, handed down through countless generations, is etched with runes of protection and endurance, shimmering faintly with the power of his ancestors. Each dent and scratch tells a tale of battles fought and grudges avenged. Hergar seeks to expand further west and south to increase his influence, there are very few greenskin tribes this side of the vaults, but the skaven are in over abundance, which is why expansion has to be carefully planned. The skaven have ignored the insignificant hold for now, but if they expand too quickly, they might draw the skaven into a war the dwarfs cannot win, even with their human allies. Hergar himself is a traditionalist, as the hold can ill afford the maintenance of guns and cannons, and relies heavily on his quarrelers and and grudge throwers to make up for their lack of firepower.

Durmin Ironscribe is the spiritual and arcane heart of Карак-Экcьфілаз. As Master of the hold’s ancient forge, he wields the sacred art of rune-craft, inscribing powerful runes upon weapons, armour, and even the gates of the hold itself. A figure of immense wisdom, Durmin’s long beard is braided with threads of silver and gold, each braid symbolising a rune he has mastered over a lifetime of study and devotion. A staunch guardian of tradition, Durmin ensures that the ancient lore of the Dwarfs is neither lost nor diluted, passing it down to the next generation with unwavering precision. Карак-Экcьфілаз possesses few Runesmiths, and those it does have are trained extensively, for only the finest may carry the sacred craft. Owing to the hold’s scarcity of rich ores, Durmin has become a master of his craft, capable of inscribing runes even upon common iron, imbuing it with strength and resilience to rival gromril itself. Under his watchful eye, even the humblest blade may become a weapon worthy of song and saga.

Lord and reigning Champion of Карак-Экcьфілаз, Durnik Stonefist is a warrior of unmatched prowess and a living legend among his kin. Towering over most Dwarfs, his formidable frame is the result of decades of unrelenting training and hard-won battles. Each year, Карак-Экcьфілаз hosts the famed Clash of Clans, a brutal contest of strength in which only the lords of the clans may compete. Durnik has claimed victory thirteen years in a row, his dominance undisputed. Though the King is permitted to take part, he has abstained ever since the infamous Broken Skull incident, an event spoken of in hushed tones and grim chuckles, choosing instead to preside over the games as host.

Master of the mines within Карак-Экcьфілаз, Finn Deepdelver is charged with the oversight and safe expansion of the hold’s tunnels through the Vaults, as well as the establishment of new mines in search of precious ore. Though possessed of a gruff and taciturn demeanour, Finn holds a deep and abiding care for his miners. He has, on more than one occasion, placed himself in grave danger to pull his kin from the rubble of collapsed shafts or to fend off sudden greenskin ambushes in the dark.

Lord Brogg Ironthane is a paragon of Dwarfen resilience, a stalwart defender of Карак-Экcьфілаз who commands respect with every measured step of his iron-shod boots. His towering frame, by Dwarfen standards, is encased in a suit of armour so intricately wrought, it is said to have taken a full century to complete. Brogg’s presence upon the battlefield serves as a rallying cry for his kin; his booming voice, like the tolling of a great bell, stirs even the most battle-weary warriors to rise and fight anew. In the aftermath of battle, he is often found within the great halls of Карак-Экcьфілаз, recounting tales of the ancestors and raising a tankard in their honour. Yet, behind his steely exterior lies a heart weighed down by the losses his clan has endured through centuries of unrelenting war.

Dwinbar Underforge, the Flamebearer of Карак-Экcьфілаз, is a figure wreathed in both mystery and fire. His long, braided beard, streaked with the ash-grey of age, is bound with golden clasps shaped like tongues of flame. His armour, an intricate mosaic of bronze and steel, shimmers with the heat of runes. These ancient and potent inscriptions allow him to channel fire itself in battle, reducing his foes to cinders with a single swing of his hammer. Born into the Underforge line, Dwinbar’s affinity for flame and metal was evident from a young age. As a youth, he spent countless hours in the forges of Карак-Экcьфілаз, learning the secrets of the ancestors who first mastered the art of binding fire to steel. Despite his fiery demeanour, Dwinbar is a deeply introspective Dwarf. He often retreats to the Forge of Ancestral Flames, a sacred chamber within Карак-Экcьфілаз, to commune with the spirits of his forebears. There, he crafts weapons and armour of unparalleled quality, each piece imbued with the enduring essence of his lineage.

Fimbur Frostbeard, the Winter’s Sentinel, is the living embodiment of the cold, unyielding strength of the mountains. His beard, white as freshly fallen snow, flows down to his belt, secured with bands of silver and frost-crystals. His armour gleams with an icy sheen, its surface perpetually cold to the touch. Crafted from a rare alloy found only in the deepest mines of Kraka Drak, it is said to be impervious to both flame and frost. Fimbur wields a warhammer forged from glacial ice and bound with runes of eternal cold. When swung, the weapon leaves a trail of frost in the air, and its impact can freeze foes solid. His mastery of the chill extends beyond his weapon; his very presence seems to leech warmth from the air, sapping the strength of his enemies and fortifying his kin. Fimbur yearns to one day return north to help his kin fight against the armies of chaos.

Grimbold Stonecleaver, the Shield of the Deep, is a towering figure whose very presence exudes an aura of unshakeable strength. His beard, a cascade of dark grey, is woven with iron clasps bearing the sigils of his clan. His armour is a marvel of engineering, layered with interlocking plates that offer unmatched protection without sacrificing mobility. His shield is as tall as a man and as unyielding as the mountains themselves. Grimbold’s weapon of choice is a massive handaxe, a relic passed down through his family for generations. The blade, etched with runes of impact, is capable of splitting even the hardest stone with a single swing. In battle, Grimbold is a bastion of defence, standing firm against even the most ferocious assaults. His shield wall is the stuff of legend, a formation that has withstood countless sieges and charges.

Lord Guttri Ironsunder is a figure of grim determination and unrelenting resolve, embodying the stoic endurance of the Dwarfs of Карак-Экcьфілаз. His beard, black as coal and streaked with the grey of age, is bound with iron clasps shaped like shattered anvils, symbols of his clan’s enduring strength in the face of adversity. Guttri’s armour is forged from fragments of ancient Dwarfen artefacts, reforged into a suit that gleams with a dull, unyielding sheen. Each plate is etched with runes of defiance, granting him resilience against both blade and sorcery. Born into the Ironsunder line, Guttri has always borne the weight of his ancestors’ grudges with fierce pride. His clan, renowned for its mastery of siegecraft and fortification, has long served as the backbone of Карак-Экcьфілаз’s defences. Guttri himself has overseen the construction of countless battlements and redoubts, each a silent testament to his skill, foresight, and unbreakable will.

Lord Thungi Stonehammer is a towering figure among the Dwarfs of Карак-Экcьфілаз, his presence as solid and enduring as the mountains themselves. His beard, a deep auburn streaked with silver, flows down to his chest, bound with clasps of polished granite and gold. His armour is a masterpiece of Dwarfen craftsmanship, its surface engraved with intricate depictions of mountain ranges and ancient runes of stability. Thungi’s weapon of choice is a massive warhammer hewn from a single block of enchanted granite. The hammer’s head is inscribed with runes of impact, each blow capable of shattering stone or hurling foes from their feet. Thungi is a deeply spiritual Dwarf, often found within the Temple of Grungni, where he offers prayers in thanks for the bounty of the mountains. His steadfast faith and enduring wisdom make him a trusted advisor to King Hergar Панцыр-Сталь, and his voice carries great weight in the council chambers of Карак-Экcьфілаз.

King Skag Hammerfist, the stalwart ruler of Карак-Гантук, is a Dwarf of unmatched resilience and strength. His massive frame is clad in a suit of ancient gromril armour, adorned with runes of warding and endurance, forged by the finest Runesmiths of the hold in ages past. His beard, a deep iron-grey streaked with white, is braided and bound with silver rings, each a mark of a great victory or a defining moment in his reign. Skag’s weapon is a colossal warhammer etched with runes of shattering and impact. Passed down through generations of kings, it becomes in Skag’s hands the symbol of his unbreakable will. On the battlefield, King Skag is a force of nature, his hammer crushing through armour and bone alike, his booming voice rallying the warriors of Gantuk to fight with unyielding resolve.

Runelord Thrandin Stoneforge is one of the most revered figures in Карак-Гантук, a master of the ancient and sacred art of rune magic. His beard, long and fiery red, is bound with golden clasps shaped like anvils, and his eyes burn with the intensity of a forge-fire. Thrandin’s armour is etched with runes of warding and spell-breaking, rendering him a bulwark against sorcery and the dark arts. He wields a rune-inscribed hammer of formidable power, each swing unleashes a burst of searing energy, capable of sunder­ing enemy lines or burning through enchanted barriers. Ever at his side is the Book of the Forge, an ancient tome containing the secrets of his craft, its pages consulted with reverence before new runes are inscribed or their potent magics invoked.

Lord Brond Deepstone, master of Карак-Гантук’s mines, is a grizzled veteran of countless expeditions into the mountain’s shadowed depths. His beard, black as coal and streaked with silver, is bound with steel clasps shaped like pickaxes. Brond’s armour is reinforced with stone-plated segments and etched with runes of fortitude, enabling him to endure the crushing pressures of the deep earth. He wields a colossal pickaxe forged from enchanted steel, capable of cleaving through stone and enemy armour with equal ease. On the battlefield, Brond strikes with the precision of a master miner, each blow measured, deliberate, and devastating, aimed to exploit the weaknesses of his foes with ruthless efficiency.

Lord Durn Wavebreaker is the stalwart commander of Карак-Гантук’s shieldwall, a figure of iron resolve and unyielding discipline. His beard, dark brown and streaked with grey, is braided and bound with bronze clasps shaped like shields, symbols of his unwavering commitment to defence. Durn’s armour is engraved with runes of protection, rendering him all but impervious to harm. He bears a towering shield reinforced with Gromril, its surface scarred by a hundred battles. In the crucible of war, Durn leads from the front, his shield the anchor of the Dwarfen line, his axe hewing down any foe bold enough to test his mettle. A resolute defender of Карак-Гантук, Durn’s leadership has turned back countless invasions. His warriors follow him without question, for they know he will never falter, never yield, and never leave a comrade behind.

Lord Harrin Goldbeard is the master of Карак-Гантук’s treasury, a shrewd and calculating Dwarf with a gaze sharp as a jeweller’s lens and a mind honed for matters of coin and craft. His beard, a gleaming cascade of gold, is bound with rings of platinum and studded with gemstones, each a testament to his success and status. His armour, inscribed with runes of prosperity and resilience, marks him as the guardian of the hold’s wealth and fiscal strength. Harrin wields an ornate axe forged from enchanted gold, its blade etched with runes of sharpness, both a symbol of his authority and a weapon of deadly efficiency. Though his focus lies with the ledgers and vaults, Harrin is no stranger to battle; when the time comes, his strikes are measured, precise, and lethal.

Lord Kargan Ironheart is the Warden of Карак-Гантук’s gates, a grim, unyielding Dwarf who bears his duty with unflinching resolve. His beard, black streaked with grey, is bound with iron clasps shaped like ancient keys, symbolising his role as keeper of the hold. Kargan’s armour, engraved with runes of endurance, renders him near-immovable, an unbreakable bulwark against all who would assail the gates. He wields a massive maul, forged to crush those foolish enough to test the strength of Карак-Гантук’s defences. Tireless and ever-watchful, Kargan inspects the fortifications daily, ensuring that every wall stands firm and every gate is sealed tight against the darkness beyond.

Lord Garin Thunderhammer is the master of Карак-Гантук’s artillery, a position he upholds with the zeal of a true engineer and the precision of a seasoned tactician. His beard, grey and flecked with soot, is bound with clasps shaped like cannonballs, a mark of his lifelong devotion to the art of war. Garin’s armour, reinforced with runes of resistance, shields him from the blasts and shrapnel that accompany his volatile craft. He wields a warhammer forged from Gromril and etched with runes of shattering, the hammer strikes with the concussive force of a cannonball. Each blow lands with a resounding boom, splintering shields and shaking enemy ranks to their core. As a commander, Garin is both meticulous and inventive, ever seeking new ways to harness the destructive might of his war machines. Yet his fury is legendary, swift and unrelenting, should his beloved artillery be misused, neglected, or placed in jeopardy.

Lord Throngrim Anvilborn is a living legend among the Dwarfs of Карак-Гантук, a warrior whose name is spoken with reverence and awe in every hearth and hall. His beard, a deep brown bound with bronze clasps shaped like axes, reflects his status as a master of war. Throngrim’s armour is a masterpiece of Dwarfen craftsmanship: a thick suit composed of interlocking layers of iron and steel, engraved with runes of protection and strength, enabling him to endure even the most brutal of onslaughts. He wields a rune-inscribed axe, striking with terrifying speed and precision. Etched with runes of sharpness and fury, the weapon carves through enemy ranks as if they were parchment. Throngrim’s fighting style is a fearsome blend of discipline and savagery, refined through countless battles against Greenskins, Skaven, and the darkspawn of Chaos. As a leader, Throngrim is both unyielding and inspirational. His thunderous voice echoes across the battlefield, stirring the hearts of his kin and urging them to fight with the wrath of the ancestors. His presence alone is enough to rally wavering lines, and his deeds are immortalised in sagas and stone within the halls of Карак-Гантук. Off the battlefield, Throngrim is a staunch traditionalist, fiercely devoted to the ancient customs and values of his people. He dedicates his time to training the next generation of warriors, ensuring that the martial legacy of Карак-Гантук remains as enduring as the mountains themselves.

Lord Dorrin Stonehearth is the steadfast keeper of Карак-Гантук’s hearth and home, a noble whose focus lies in the defence and prosperity of the hold’s inner sanctums. His beard, a rich auburn streaked with grey, is adorned with clasps shaped like hearthstones, symbolising his unwavering commitment to the safety and well-being of his kin. Dorrin’s armour is a marvel of Dwarfen craftsmanship, inscribed with runes of resilience and fortitude, ensuring he stands firm against any threat that dares breach the hold’s walls. He wields a rune-etched warhammer that embodies the enduring spirit of Карак-Гантук’s hearthfires. Imbued with runes of striking and endurance, the weapon delivers crushing blows while imbuing nearby allies with a sense of unity and steadfast resolve. As a leader, Dorrin is pragmatic and fiercely protective of his folk. He oversees the daily workings of the hold, its forges, granaries, and mines, ensuring all run with Dwarfen precision and order. In times of war, he commands the Hearthguard: a veteran unit of warriors sworn to defend the inner halls and sacred places of the hold. Dorrin is deeply respected for his wisdom and patience, qualities that make him a trusted counsellor to King Skag Hammerfist. His voice carries weight in the council chambers, where he champions strategies that temper aggression with the enduring preservation of Карак-Гантук’s strength.

Lord Varrik Dúmdrengi is a figure of grim determination and searing resolve, a Daemon Slayer who has risen to a position of leadership not through lineage, but by deeds of unmatched savagery and valour. His beard, once a proud auburn, now burns a fiery orange, dyed in the Slayer tradition and bound with iron clasps shaped like runic flames. His bare chest is a testament to his trials, marked with scars and tattoos, each a record of a mighty foe vanquished in his relentless quest for a glorious death. Varrik bears a colossal axe inscribed with ancient runes of destruction. The weapon is said to burn with an inner fire, its edge capable of cleaving through the armoured hides of Chaos champions and even the ethereal flesh of daemons. His strikes land with terrifying force, driven by a Slayer’s unyielding fury and a burning thirst for redemption. Though an unconventional lord, Varrik commands the respect of his kin through sheer force of will and the magnitude of his deeds. He leads a grim brotherhood of Slayers who have sworn themselves to his cause, oath-bound warriors united in vengeance, bound to walk the path of ruin until their doom is earned. Varrik’s presence in Карак-Гантук is both a source of inspiration and unease. To many, he embodies the very essence of Dwarfen wrath and resilience, a living legend who will not bow, even before death itself.

Alrik Ranulfsson is regarded as something of an oddity, even amongst a race as steeped in custom and tradition as the Dwarfs, for his near-fanatical devotion to the ways of his forebears. Despite the increasing need to deal with other races for trade and diplomacy, Alrik has held fast to the ancient customs of his people, refusing to yield an inch to modernisation. His armies are composed of warriors and Ironbreakers, supported by Quarrellers and Grudge-Throwers, echoing the proud formations of old. He has little time for newfangled contraptions such as Flame Cannons and Gyrocopters, viewing them as unproven distractions from tried-and-true methods of war. Alrik is even more of a traditionalist than his father, Ranulf, and has taken it upon himself to pursue the settling of every wrong inscribed within Карак-Хірн’s Book of Grudges. With grim determination, he wages war against Greenskins, Skaven, and even Elves, demanding recompense in blood for ancient slights and betrayals. While all Dwarfs are taught the bitterness of grievance, few pursue vengeance with the same relentless fervour as Alrik. He has already struck out an entire volume of grudges, but the book is thick, and many pages still remain.

Prince Gorrin Alriksson, son of King Alrik Ranulfsson, stands apart from many of his kin through temperament as much as deed. Where his father is stern and steeped in the old ways, Gorrin is possessed of a more even-handed nature, an inheritance from his mother, whose calm judgement and open-mindedness left a lasting mark upon the young prince as he grew up. Gorrin bears the heavy burden of representing his hold to the outside world. Unlike many of his kin, he does not look down upon other races. While never forgetful of the grudges his people carry, he is willing to speak with Elves and treat with Humans, seeing in them not just allies of convenience, but peoples with whom mutual respect, and even friendship, might be forged. Though some in the council chambers grumble at his modern learnings, none can deny that Gorrin’s efforts have opened valuable trade routes, eased tensions with nearby settlements, and brought honour to Карак-Хірн through his skill in negotiation. Calm where his father is fierce, measured where others bristle, Gorrin may yet be the future his hold needs in a world ever darkening with war.

Hamnir once fought as a mercenary in Tilea, hired by a noble who laid claim to the lands of a rival. The wars of the southern realms are often petty and short-lived, little more than skirmishes or single-day battles, but they are no less real for it. Steel is drawn, lives are lost, and reputations are forged in blood. Though many dismiss these conflicts as play-fighting for the bored sons of the nobility, the deaths are no less real. Lords from across the Old World send their heirs to the Tilean wars to earn their scars and temper their pride, and the Dwarfs are no exception. Hamnir was one such noble. Arrogant and untested, he entered the fray seeking glory, but found instead the hard lessons of humility, hardship, and brotherhood in battle. His years in Tilea were not merely for experience, but for the forging of a truer character, one that understood the weight of command, the sting of loss, and the value of comradeship.

Skalf Ironpeak is a Dwarf Lord of towering stature and indomitable will. His beard, braided into intricate patterns, gleams with silver and gold, a testament to his high standing as the very pinnacle of Dwarven nobility. Clad in a suit of rune-inscribed Gromril armour, Skalf embodies the unyielding resilience of his kin, standing firm against any threat to his hold. He wields a great hammer forged in the deepest forges of Карак-Хірн, a weapon of ancient power. Its runes shimmer with arcane might, and each strike delivers a crushing blow capable of breaking even the most formidable of foes. Yet Skalf is more than a warrior, he is a diplomat and steward of his people, balancing the needs of Карак-Хірн with the interests of the greater Dwarven realms and, at times, even those of the Empire. When a trading caravan or emissary manages to brave the perilous mountain paths leading to Карак-Хірн, they are often greeted by Skalf himself, flanked by a retinue of honour guards, a gesture of both hospitality and strength.

Runelord Drumin Stonecarver is the revered master of Карак-Хірн’s runesmithing halls, a venerable Dwarf whose command of rune magic is unmatched across the mountains. His beard, streaked with white, is bound with bands of gold inscribed with ancestral symbols, while his eyes burn with the fire of centuries spent in relentless study and sacred toil. Drumin’s armour is adorned with warding runes that shimmer faintly with a bluish hue, a quiet but constant testament to the power of his craft. He wields a mighty rune-hammer, used both upon the anvil and upon the battlefield. The head of the hammer is etched with runes of Breaking and Binding, allowing Drumin to shatter enemy enchantments with a single blow or to bolster the resolve of his kin when the tide of battle threatens to turn.

Lord Durrin Granitefist is the stalwart commander of Карак-Хірн’s Ironbreakers, a seasoned warrior whose courage and martial prowess are the stuff of legend. His beard is dark and thick, braided with clasps of tempered steel, while his gromril armour bears the scars of countless campaigns fought beneath the mountain’s shadow. Durrin wields a rune-etched axe, its edge capable of sundering even the most formidable of defences. In battle, he leads with unshakable resolve, forming an unbreakable wall of shields that has repelled countless greenskin hordes and Beastmen incursions. Though gruff and uncompromising, Durrin is fiercely loyal to his king and kin, earning the unwavering respect of all who march beneath his banner.

Vikram Grimflame is a Daemon Slayer whose deeds have secured him a place in the annals of Карак-Хірн’s storied history. His fiery orange hair and beard, bound with iron bands, stand in stark contrast to the grim resolve etched into his battle-worn features. Vikram wields a massive rune-axe, its blade inscribed with runes of flame, capable of incinerating daemonic foes with every strike. His body bears the marks of countless battles, scarred flesh and sacred tattoos, each one a testament to a victory won against the unholy forces of Chaos.

Manrak Ironspike, a venerable lord of Карак-Хірн, stands as the unyielding guardian of the hold’s southern approaches. Renowned for his iron resolve and masterful defensive strategies, Manrak has weathered countless assaults from Greenskin warbands and Beastman raiders amidst the rugged peaks. Clad in ancestral armour engraved with intricate runes of fortitude, he bears a massive shield forged from meteoric iron and wields a rune-etched warhammer that has laid low innumerable foes. Though ever the stalwart defender, Manrak harbours a simmering hatred for the Ogres who prowl the mountain passes. He dreams of one day leading a great muster to drive them out entirely, reclaiming the lost trade routes and securing Карак-Хірн’s supremacy over the southern mountains.

Durin Rockhewer is a masterful miner and renowned delver, famed for uncovering long-lost vaults and hidden chambers deep within the roots of Карак-Хірн. As Keeper of the Lost Vaults, Durin oversees the mining expeditions that fuel the hold’s wealth and keep its forges burning with unyielding fire.
