His appearance is as rugged as the mountains he carves. His beard, streaked with grey and coal dust, is braided with bands of silver, each one marking a discovery of note. He wears a helm hewn from black granite and a cloak fashioned from the hides of cave-beasts, tokens of his many forays into the forgotten deeps. Durin is a deeply superstitious soul, often seeking the counsel of Runelords before embarking on major delvings. He holds a firm belief that the mountains whisper to those willing to listen. and more than once, his uncanny intuition has spared his crews from cave-ins, lurking beasts, or worse.

Balin Stormpeak is a formidable figure within Карак-Хірн, renowned for his mastery of mountain warfare and an unyielding will as enduring as the peaks he defends. For decades, Balin has safeguarded the vital trade routes and treacherous mountain passes that link Карак-Хірн to the wider world. Though a battle-hardened warrior, Balin is also a tactician of considerable reputation. He is a master of ambush and terrain manipulation, expertly turning the unforgiving landscape of the mountains to his advantage. Many would-be invaders have found their doom amidst rockfalls and hidden kill-zones, their plans undone by Balin’s cunning stratagems. Despite his martial prowess, Balin is a staunch advocate of diplomacy and trade, recognising the strategic value of Карак-Хірн’s role as a bastion of commerce. He is often called upon to mediate disputes between neighbouring holds and human settlements, earning him respect even beyond the mountain's shadow.

Kazran Grimbrow is the King of Карак-Ізор and is a formidable figure among the nobility, his thick, grey-streaked beard braided with silver clasps, and his brow set in a perpetual scowl of grim determination. Clad in gleaming gromril armour inscribed with runes of resilience and prosperity, Kazran bears himself with the solemn weight of a king whose every decree shapes the destiny of his hold. His crown, a masterwork of silver and gold set with diamonds, is said to have been forged by the first Runelords of Карак-Ізор, an enduring symbol of his clan’s unbroken lineage. Kazran wields an ancient rune-axe passed down through generations of Clan Ізоргрунг’s rulers. The weapon serves as both a symbol of kingship and an instrument of war, its blade etched with runes of sharpness and vengeance that gleam with an otherworldly light. In battle, Kazran is a fearsome sight, his strikes precise and unrelenting, his mere presence enough to stir the hearts of his warriors and drive them to renewed feats of valour.

Lord Thori Goldhammer is a stalwart lord of Карак-Ізор, a master of both diplomacy and war. He oversees the extraction and refinement of precious metals and gemstones, safeguarding the prosperity of his kin. Thori’s armour is a dazzling masterpiece of gromril, inlaid with silver and gold filigree, a testament to Карак-Ізор’s wealth and craftsmanship. His weapon of choice is a rune-axe of peerless make, rumoured to strike with the precision of a jeweller’s chisel. Though a warrior of renown, Thori is also a shrewd negotiator. He has forged enduring alliances with nearby holds and human realms, ensuring Карак-Ізор remains a vital nexus of trade and a rival in influence to Карак-Хірн. Yet he is no stranger to battle; his axe has slain countless Greenskins and Skaven who dared encroach upon the hold’s treasures. His leadership is defined by balance, tempered by wisdom, yet unyielding in the face of adversity.

Brokk Silverwright is the venerable Runelord of Карак-Ізор, a figure of immense reverence and awe. With a beard as white as freshly fallen snow and eyes that gleam like molten silver, Brokk embodies the ancient wisdom of the Dwarfen race. Clad in rune-etched gromril armour, he bears a mighty hammer that serves as an extension of his indomitable will. Brokk’s mastery of rune magic is the stuff of legend, and many of Карак-Ізор’s most prized heirlooms bear the mark of his craftsmanship. His presence on the battlefield is as heartening as it is decisive, his runes of warding and resilience have turned the tide of countless engagements. Despite his great age, Brokk remains a staunch defender of the hold, often marching alongside his kin to ensure his runes are wielded with the honour and purpose for which they were forged.

Hugnir Firemane is a figure of grim legend within Карак-Ізор, a Daemon Slayer whose fiery beard and burning gaze are said to mirror the fury of the Ancestors themselves. Once a proud warrior of the hold, Hugnir took the Slayer’s Oath after failing to protect his kin during a Skaven incursion into the lower mines. Since that day, he has sought redemption through battle, carving a path of destruction through the enemies of Карак-Ізор. Clad in nothing but his tattoos and a rune-etched greataxe, Hugnir’s presence is a terrifying sight to behold. His axe glows with a baleful light, its runes flaring with deadly power as they bite into daemonic flesh. Though he has forsaken all claim to leadership, Hugnir’s deeds inspire both awe and dread among his kin. He stands as a living reminder of the price of failure, and of the unyielding strength of Dwarfen resolve. Many whisper that Hugnir’s final battle shall be one for the ages, a clash that will see him redeemed in the eyes of the Ancestors, or lost forever to the annals of history as a legend without equal.

Drakk Gunmarsson is the stalwart guardian of Карак-Ізор’s western territories, a region often threatened by Greenskin raiders and marauding Beastmen. His thick, craggy brow gives him a perpetually stern look, and his braided auburn beard is streaked with soot from countless battles fought in defence of the hold. Drakk is a born warrior, clad in rune-inscribed gromril plate that has withstood the blows of trolls and the claws of Chaos beasts alike. His weapon of choice is a colossal rune-axe that hums with runes of cleaving and thunder, capable of rending even the hardiest foe in twain. Renowned for his mastery of defensive warfare, Drakk has time and again turned narrow mountain passes into slaughterfields for invading armies. Though gruff and taciturn, his loyalty to King Kazran and his love for Карак-Ізор are beyond reproach. To Drakk, the hold’s walls are sacred, and he will fight to his last breath to ensure they are never breached.

Gorrik Flintshield is the indomitable Captain of Карак-Ізор’s elite shieldwall regiment. His name is spoken with reverence by the warriors under his command and with dread by the Greenskins who have faced him in battle. Gorrik’s stout frame is encased in gromril plate, and his shield is a massive slab of rune-inscribed steel, said to have turned aside the crushing blow of a Wyvern’s tail. His weapon of choice is a hefty warhammer, forged to deliver devastating strikes that shatter both armour and bone. A veteran of countless engagements, Gorrik is famed for his unyielding resolve and tactical acumen. He has held narrow mountain passes against overwhelming odds, his shieldwall standing firm as the mountains themselves. His leadership is direct and uncompromising, demanding discipline and valour from his warriors. Yet, his loyalty to his kin and his hold is absolute. Off the battlefield, Gorrik is a staunch traditionalist, deeply devoted to the ancestors and the preservation of Dwarfen customs. He frequently confers with King Kazran Grimbrow on matters of defence and military strategy, ensuring that Карак-Ізор remains an impenetrable bastion against the foes that try to assail it.

Barik Stonehelm is the master of Карак-Ізор’s Forgeworks, a labyrinthine complex of anvils, workshops, and roaring furnaces where the hold’s most formidable war machines and firearms are wrought. His thick black beard is singed at the edges, and his hands are perpetually stained with soot and oil, a testament to a lifetime of toil amidst flame and steel. Barik’s armour is a patchwork of riveted steel plates and reinforced leather, festooned with tools, cogs, and mechanisms. His famed mechanical gauntlet, powered by concealed gears and counterweights, is a marvel of his own invention. He wields a masterfully engineered handgun that fires explosive rounds, and he carries an assortment of grenades and experimental devices, each capable of altering the course of battle in an instant. His ingenuity has earned him the grudging respect of even the most conservative Runelords, and his creations, from flame-belching cannons to armoured gyrocopters, stand at the forefront of Карак-Ізор’s defences. Though gruff and often irascible, Barik is fiercely protective of both his kin and his craft. He insists on testing his inventions personally, and has been known to lead his fellow engineers into battle to ensure their machines perform to exacting standards. Barik’s relentless innovation and battlefield prowess have secured his place in the annals of Карак-Ізор’s history as one of its most gifted and unorthodox minds.

Thorik Stonebrow is the Keeper of the Oathstone, a sacred relic of Карак-Ізор that symbolises the unbreakable vows of its people. A towering figure among his kin, Thorik’s beard is streaked with grey, and his craggy features bear the weight of centuries of unflinching duty. His armour, adorned with the runes of the ancestors, gleams with a dull, battle-worn sheen, and his warhammer is a fearsome relic said to shatter the resolve of even the most steadfast foes. Thorik’s role as Keeper is both ceremonial and martial. He presides over the swearing of oaths, ensuring that promises made to the hold and its king are neither spoken lightly nor forgotten. In battle, he is a resolute presence, often standing at the heart of the shieldwall, his voice a booming reminder of the vows his warriors have sworn. Honourable and unyielding, Thorik is driven by a deep-rooted sense of duty. He is known to hold grudges with an iron grip, pursuing retribution for any slight against his hold or his kin with relentless resolve. Though his demeanour is stern and uncompromising, Thorik is deeply respected by his peers. His unwavering devotion to Карак-Ізор and its ancient traditions embodies the very essence of Dwarven resilience.

Skorri Ironvein is the indomitable commander of Карак-Ізор’s elite warriors, tasked with patrolling the lower tunnels and mines of the hold. His broad frame and weathered visage speak of a lifetime spent beneath the mountain, where danger lurks in every shadow. Skorri’s armour is a masterwork of function and craftsmanship, reinforced with thick gromril plates and etched with runes of endurance, built to withstand the crushing blows of subterranean foes. His axe, perfectly balanced for the tight confines of the tunnels, has claimed countless Greenskin and Skaven lives. Skorri’s leadership is defined by pragmatism and adaptability. He knows the labyrinthine depths of Карак-Ізор as others know the lines of their own hands, able to read the stone like a map. His warriors trust him implicitly, knowing his calm demeanour and sharp instincts have saved them from ambushes and cave-ins more times than they can recall. Off duty, Skorri is a private and contemplative figure, often found in the lower halls inspecting the mines or sharpening his axe. Though he rarely partakes in the revelries of the upper halls, his loyalty to Карак-Ізор is beyond question, and his name is spoken with reverence among those who brave the dark depths.

Borri Gembeard is the Master Prospector of Карак-Ізор, a title of great prestige in a hold famed for its abundance of precious metals and gemstones. His braided beard glitters with embedded jewels, each one a testament to his unmatched skill in uncovering the mountain’s hidden wealth. His pickaxe serves both as a tool and a weapon, its haft inlaid with silver runes of precision and strength, while his armour gleams with polished copper and gold plates, reflecting the riches he has brought forth. Borri is a Dwarf of boundless curiosity and relentless determination. He has led countless expeditions into uncharted tunnels, his keen eye and deep knowledge of geology uncovering rich veins of ore and gemstone that have greatly enriched the hold. Though not a frontline warrior, Borri is no stranger to combat, having defended his prospecting parties against Skaven raiders and the many beasts that dwell in the deep places of the world. In the council chambers, Borri’s counsel is highly valued; his insights into the mountain’s resources are key to Карак-Ізор’s economic strength and strategic planning. Despite his wealth and renown, he remains grounded, often found in the common halls recounting tales of peril and discovery over a well-earned tankard of ale. To his kin, Borri Gembeard represents the enduring bond between the Dwarfs and the mountains they call home, a living symbol of resilience, industry, and ancestral pride.

King Skalf Redbeard is a ruler caught between tradition and diplomacy, a stout and battle-hardened Dwarf whose rule has seen both prosperity and strife. Clad in masterfully forged gromril plate and bearing the axe, Oathkeeper, a relic of his line. Skalf stands as a beacon of stubborn resilience and pragmatic wisdom. His namesake beard, once the fiery red of a forge’s heart, has begun to grey with age. Centuries ago, King Skalf did what few Dwarf rulers would dare, he brokered trade agreements with the Wood Elves of Атэль Лорэн. While many of his kin scowled at the notion of dealing with the fickle Asrai, Skalf saw opportunity. Timber from the Elves strengthened the hold’s construction efforts, while Dwarfen steel and crafted wares found their way into Elven hands. The accords brought wealth and stability to Карак-Каферкамаз, and for a time, both races benefited from a rare peace in the Vaults. But the years have not been kind to these ties. Old grudges and shifting alliances have strained the fragile peace. The Asrai grow ever more secretive and untrusting, while Dwarfs of the hold grumble that their generosity has been met with aloof disdain. Skalf, for all his efforts, walks a narrow path, striving to uphold the accords lest both sides descend into open war. He is wise enough to know that a single wrong word, broken promise, or bloodied axe could undo centuries of uneasy cooperation. Yet, should the Elves betray their trust, should they draw first blood, then Skalf Redbeard will not hesitate. The oaths of peace will be cast into the forge, and Карак-Каферкамаз shall march to war. Until that day comes, the King stands firm, balancing the legacy of his rule upon the edge of a finely honed axe.

Born beneath the vaulted halls of Карак-Каферкамаз, Prince Elmador Skalfsson was raised in the shadow of his father, King Skalf Redbeard, a ruler known for his diplomacy and pragmatism. But where his father saw opportunity, Elmador saw compromise, and where Skalf sought peace, Elmador seethed with resentment. He was a child of war, raised on the stories of Elven treachery and the endless struggles against the beastmen and raiders of the underway. To him, the treaties with the Wood Elves were not a mark of wisdom, but a stain upon Dwarfen honour. Clad in finely crafted gromril armour, adorned with the rune-etched pauldrons of Clan Skalfsson, Elmador is every inch the warrior-prince. His warhammer was forged in defiance of the Asrai, a symbol of his belief that Dwarfs should not barter with those who live by deception and magic. He leads patrols into the northern reaches of the hold, watching the tree line with suspicion, ever wary of an Elven knife in the dark. To his credit, Elmador does not defy his father openly. He is a Dwarf of discipline and respect, and his loyalty to King Skalf remains unquestioned. But deep within, he waits for the day when he will take the throne, when he can right the wrongs of the past and cast aside the treaties his father signed. The Wood Elves, in his mind, are fickle and faithless, and he believes that sooner or later, they will turn on the Dwarfs as they always have. While others hope for continued peace, Elmador prepares for war. He strengthens the hold’s defences, gathers warriors to his banner, and ensures that should the Elves so much as step beyond their borders, Карак-Каферкамаз will be ready. He is a hammer waiting to fall, and when it does, the echoes of his wrath may shake the Vaults themselves.

Once a proud and decorated thane of Карак-Каферкамаз, Kazran Firebrand was a name spoken with both reverence and sorrow. He had stood as a shield for his kin, his axe breaking many foes upon the bloodied stone of the underway. His greatest failure came when the hold was beset by a monstrous daemon of Tzeentch, a creature of ever-shifting flesh and sorcery that twisted reality itself. Kazran led the charge against it, his warriors fighting with unyielding Dwarfen might, but in the end, the beast was vanquished only at a terrible cost. His own brother, Durn, fell to its sorcery, his body turning to lifeless crystal before Kazran ’s very eyes. Wracked with grief and bound by the burden of shame, Kazran did what many before him had done, he cast aside his name, his wealth, and his place within the hold, taking up the oath of the Slayer. Yet his path was not of blind fury; he sought vengeance upon daemons and every other vile thing that crawled from the depths of Chaos. He fights wherever the taint of the Dark Gods is found, his great axe runed and reforged with burning glyphs, turning the flesh of daemons to ash with each strike. His once-proud golden hair is now a wild mane of fire, bound in the ancient oath-locks of Grimnir, his body adorned with scars both physical and spiritual. Though his name is still whispered with respect in Карак-Каферкамаз, he has no home, no clan, no kin, only the path to atonement, and the promise of one day meeting his doom in battle.

The forges of Карак-Каферкамаз burn hot under the watchful gaze of Runelord Grumli Runesoul, one of the most respected and formidable runesmiths of the Vaults. To him, runes are not mere tools, but the sacred words of the Ancestor Gods, the very essence of Dwarfen might and endurance. In the face of war, it is his duty to bind steel with the strength of the mountain, and to ensure that the warriors of Карак-Каферкамаз go into battle clad in gromril-wrought protection, infused with the oldest magics of the Dawi. Unlike many of his peers who remain within their forges, Grumli is known to take to the field of battle, standing amidst the shieldwalls of his kin, chanting oaths of defiance as he strikes his rune-covered hammer against the earth. The very ground beneath the Dwarfs becomes as unyielding as iron, their weapons glow with runic might, and spells hurled by enemy wizards break like waves upon rock. A grim and taciturn figure, Grumli bears a deep distrust of outsiders, particularly the Wood Elves, whom he believes toy too freely with the forces of magic. He opposed the treaties of King Skalf Redbeard, arguing that Elven trickery could never be trusted, and to this day, he ensures that should the accords ever break, the warriors of Карак-Каферкамаз will be ready. His personal warhammer is a relic of the past, a weapon that once sealed the gates of the hold against an endless horde of beastmen. Now, it is wielded to break the foes of the Dawi, and to remind all who stand before him that Dwarfs are not ruled by words, but by steel, stone, and the wisdom of the Ancestors.

The underpasses and deep roads of Карак-Каферкамаз are as perilous as the wilds above, filled with the skittering menace of the Skaven, the bestial hordes of the Beastmen, and the ever-present threat of Greenskin warbands. Yet for every ambush, every attempted invasion, there stands a wall of steel and resolve in the form of Lord Borri Ironfist, Shieldmaster of the Underway, and the unyielding defender of the deep roads. Borri is a Dwarf of iron discipline, a warrior who has spent centuries battling the filth of the underground, ensuring that the lifeblood of the hold, the mines and trade routes, remains secure. He has fought in battles where the torches barely glowed, where the enemy came in tides without number, and where the only thing that held the line was the unshakable will of Dawi warriors standing shoulder to shoulder. Clad in blackened gromril plate, his shield adorned with the sigil of Карак-Каферкамаз, Borri is a warrior of unyielding endurance, a rock amidst the storm. He wields a weapon once thought lost in the depths of a collapsed tunnel, recovered only after Borri personally led an expedition into the darkest reaches of the underway to reclaim it from the skeletal remains of a long-dead Thane.

Beneath the towering peaks and sturdy walls of Карак-Каферкамаз lies a vast network of tunnels and mines that produce the ores and precious stones in the Vaults. Overseeing these treacherous depths is Lord Ulfar Stonevein, a seasoned miner turned leader, whose unmatched knowledge of the underway makes him vital to the hold’s prosperity and safety. Ulfar began his life as many Dwarfs do, with pickaxe and lantern, carving out his legacy with stone-dusted hands and sweat. It was his instinct for finding rich veins of ore and his iron resolve in defending his crews from the horrors of the deep that earned him both renown and his title. When Skaven burrowed into the lower mines, it was Ulfar who led the counterattack, wielding his twin axes with a fury that sent the ratmen scurrying back into the darkness. Though his scarred face and grizzled beard mark his years of hardship, his eyes still gleam with the hunger for discovery. His loyalty to Карак-Каферкамаз is as solid as the mountains, and he’s known to clash with more cautious lords, pushing for deeper excavations and greater risk. Yet those who follow him know that Ulfar leads from the front, where the rock is hardest and danger is greatest, he stands with his kin.

When the horns of war sound through the hold, it is Lord Hargin Emberfist who answers first, marching at the head of the Iron Guard, the elite warriors sworn to defend Карак-Каферкамаз. Known for his fiery temper and indomitable strength, Hargin has spent centuries on the battlefield, earning his name when his gauntleted fist crushed the skull of a beastman champion during a desperate last stand at Stormcleft Pass. Clad in rune-inscribed gromril armor, Hargin wields an ancient warhammer said to contain the wrath of the mountains themselves. His booming voice carries commands like thunder, and his presence on the battlefield inspires Dwarfs to stand firm, no matter how dire the odds. He has fought against Skaven hordes, Greenskin raiders, and twisting Chaos monstrosities, never retreating, never surrendering.Despite his martial prowess, Hargin is no mere brute—he is a keen tactician, respected advisor, and staunch traditionalist. He believes that the treaties with the Wood Elves have softened the hold, and frequently clashes with King Skalf Redbeard, urging a return to Dwarfen self-reliance and strength.

In times of war and peace alike, it is the strength of the home that sustains the Dawi, and Lord Brokk Stonemantle ensures that Карак-Каферкамаз’s heart remains strong. As Keeper of the Hearth and Hold, Brokk oversees the craftsmen’s guilds, the armories, and the great halls, ensuring that tradition and prosperity endure even when the world beyond the gates grows dark. Brokk’s broad shoulders and granite-like demeanor mirror the very stones of the hold itself. His beard, thick and silver, is braided with rings of honor, each marking a victory of industry and diplomacy. He is no mere frontline warrior, his greatest battles lie in council chambers and trade halls, where he negotiates with shrewd cunning and ensures the hold’s wealth flows steadily. Despite his diplomatic nature, Brokk is no friend of the Wood Elves. He remembers every slight and broken promise, and while he respects King Skalf’s efforts for peace, he trusts steel and gold far more than elven words. Yet Brokk’s calm wisdom and strategic mind make him a valued advisor.

Wherever Карак-Каферкамаз’s warriors stand their ground, Lord Kargun Stoneheart is at the forefront, an immovable wall of steel and stone. Known for his implacable nature and unshakable resolve, Kargun has become a living embodiment of Dwarfen endurance. His face, weathered and scarred, bears the marks of countless battles, and his eyes burn with the fierce light of a warrior who has never known defeat. Kargun’s name was earned in the defence of the hold’s outer tunnels, where he held a collapsing line against a tide of Beastmen for three days without rest. It is said that even when his shield arm was broken and his axe dulled, he fought on, standing amidst the bodies of the fallen until reinforcements arrived. His armour, a fortress of overlapping gromril plates, bears the scars of a thousand battles, and his shield has turned aside blows that would have felled a giant. Despite his grim and often silent demeanour, Kargun inspires fierce loyalty among his warriors. They know that where he stands, no foe will break through, and no ground will be lost. While he respects King Skalf’s efforts for diplomacy, Kargun believes peace can only be preserved through strength, and that every treaty must be backed by the might of Dwarfen steel.

Lord Hugnir Stoutshield, Guardian of the Outer Gates. As the Warden of the Outer Gates, Hugnir’s duty lies in defending the entrance to the hold itself, standing against the tide of invaders that constantly threaten the Dawi’s home. From Greenskin warbands to Beastmen raiders, Hugnir has faced them all and turned them back with unwavering resolve. A broad and imposing figure, Hugnir ’s presence on the battlefield is as immovable as the stone he defends. His gromril shield is a legendary artifact said to have withstood the hammer blows of an Orc Warlord and the sorcerous fire of a Bray-Shaman without yielding. His axe has split the skulls of countless foes and remains a symbol of his dedication to Карак-Каферкамаз. Despite his gruff demeanor and battle-hardened exterior, Hugnir is deeply loyal to King Skalf Redbeard. He has voiced his concerns about the strained relations with the Wood Elves but remains steadfast in his belief that the unity and strength of the hold come first. He views Prince Elmador’s hatred of the Asrai with caution, fearing the rashness that could lead to unnecessary conflict.

The Grey Mountains are an unforgiving land, their stone poor in ore and their slopes devoid of the riches that fuel the great holds of the World's Edge Mountains. And yet, Карак-Норн endures, not through wealth, but through the unyielding will of its king, Brokk Ironpick. A Dwarf as hard and unrelenting as the mountains themselves, King Brokk has ruled over Карак-Норн for centuries with the same iron resolve that first drove his ancestors to carve their hold from barren stone. Brokk Ironpick is a figure of grim determination. His face, lined and weathered like the cliffs of his homeland, speaks of a life spent battling both enemies and despair. His long, steel-grey beard is plaited with iron rings, and his eyes, dark and unwavering, carry the weight of every hardship his people have endured. Clad in heavy gromril armour etched with the ancient runes of endurance and fortitude, Brokk stands as a living symbol of his hold’s resilience. In battle, King Brokk is a force to behold. He wields an ancient and revered weapon, passed down through generations, a massive pickaxe forged from blackened gromril, its head covered in runes of shattering and spite. Though unconventional for a king, the weapon embodies the unyielding perseverance of Карак-Норн’s people, as well as their relentless drive to extract whatever meagre wealth their mountains might still hide. Despite his dour nature, Brokk is a king deeply respected, if not beloved, by his subjects. He demands much from his people, pushing them to dig deeper, fight harder, and endure longer than they ever thought possible. Yet he also shoulders those burdens himself, leading from the front in both war and labour. It is not uncommon to find the king in the mines alongside his kin, his iron pick striking stone with the same tireless rhythm that drives his every action. Brokk’s relationship with the neighbouring realms is one of careful pragmatism. He maintains uneasy truces with the Wood Elves of Атэль Лорэн, though his mistrust of the Asrai runs deep. The Bretonnians, with their pretensions of chivalry and their incessant squabbling, earn little more than his scorn, though he will trade with them when it serves Карак-Норн’s interests. With the Empire, there is respect, if not warmth, Brokk values their industry and discipline, but remains ever watchful for signs of human folly. As the years wear on and the mountain’s riches continue to dwindle, the weight upon Brokk Ironpick’s shoulders grows heavier. Yet still he stands, unyielding and defiant.

Few names in Карак-Норн inspire sorrow like that of Thingrim Stonefury. Once a proud Thane of his clan, Thingrim was a warrior of steadfast honour and uncompromising loyalty, until the day his hold suffered a grievous attack from the twisted forces of Chaos. In the defense of his kin, Thingrim’s only son fell to the claws of a monstrous Daemon, and with his death, something inside Thingrim broke. Consumed by grief and the need for vengeance, he shaved his head, dyed his beard in the fiery hues of shame and wrath, and took the Slayer’s oath. It's been many years since then. Thingrim , now a Daemonslayer, is a tempest of fury on the battlefield. His Runic Greataxe, Runebranded relic of his clan, strikes with the strength of an avalanche and the speed of a lightning storm. The scars that crisscross his hardened frame tell stories of battles that would have slain lesser Dwarfs, but Thingrim fights on, seeking the death he believes his failures have earned. Yet despite his oath, fate has denied him that end. Whether he stands against the Beastmen of the Grey Mountains or the raiding warbands of Greenskins, he emerges bloodied but unbroken, his defiance a symbol of Карак-Норн’s unyielding spirit. Though his presence brings unease,reminders of oaths broken and burdens borne. Thingrim Stonefury remains one of Карак-Норн’s greatest champions, his axe carving out legends even as he seeks his doom.

In the cold, mineral-poor depths of Карак-Норн, the runes burn brightest. Hakon is the master of Runecraft, his anvil a place of solemn power and his forge a sanctuary of incandescent heat. As the spiritual and magical guardian of the hold, Hakon wields the wisdom of centuries and the strength of enchanted steel. Clad in rune-etched gromril and bearing an ancient Runehammer, Hakon Emberforge is a vision of Dawi tradition and power. The air around him hums with the presence of binding runes and ancient protections, and his every strike on the battlefield leaves searing marks of warding and destruction. He is known for his stoic demeanor and his fierce dedication to the hold’s safety, channeling his craft into armaments that withstand the ravages of war and enchantments that ward against the corruption of Chaos. Despite his isolation in the forge, Hakon is no stranger to battle. When the need arises, he marches with the armies of Карак-Норн, his presence bolstering the warriors around him and his runes turning aside the deadliest of blows. He has stood at King Brokk Ironpick’s side on countless campaigns, his magic tempering the iron resolve of the hold with fire and stone.

Deep beneath Карак-Норн lies a maze of old tunnels and sealed vaults, remnants from when the Grey Mountains were thought to hold vast riches. Most have been abandoned to time and shadow, but certain vaults still flicker with torchlight. This is where Mardin Grum, known as Iron-Eye, Marches. A master of subterranean warfare and an obsessive preserver of lost history, Mardin has made it his life’s work to explore, reclaim, and restore the lower levels of the hold. His nickname comes from the heavy iron visor he wears over his eyes, a contraption of mirrored lenses and runic etchings said to help him see the traces of magical taint, structural weakness, or buried secrets. Mardin's warriors are hardened tunnel-fighters, trained to combat beasts of the dark and collapse-prone ruins. While Mardin rarely ventures topside, when he does, his voice is heavy with knowledge of things best left forgotten and dangers long entombed.

Among the lords of Карак-Норн, Dorrik stands as the embodiment of the Dawi’s most sacred tradition: the keeping and settling of grudges. As the appointed Grudgekeeper of the hold, it is Dorrik’s solemn duty to maintain the Great Book of Grudges, a task he executes with unwavering diligence and an ironclad sense of justice. With every slight against the Dawi recorded, Dorrik fights not just for victory, but for retribution, his hammer striking with the weight of millennia of unforgiven insults and unavenged deaths. Despite his grim duties, Dorrik is known for his steady hand and even temper. He advises King Brokk Ironpick with wisdom honed by decades of experience, balancing the fires of vengeance with the need for diplomacy and patience. Yet when the time comes for reckoning, none are as fierce or relentless in battle, and every foe who falls to his hammer is one step closer to settling the ancient debts of Карак-Норн. In times of peace, Dorrik is the voice of caution and resolve. In times of war, he is the storm that rights every wrong. And through it all, he remains the living memory of his people’s trials, and the iron promise that no insult shall go unanswered.

Among the grim and stubborn Dwarfs of Карак-Норн, few are more driven, or more quietly desperate, than Lord Varnik Hammerdeep. A direct descendant of one of the founding prospectors who settled the Grey Mountains on whispers of wealth, Varnik bears the burden of generations of unfulfilled promises. With pick and lantern in hand, he leads the Miners of Карак-Норн, tirelessly scouring the unstable bedrock for the motherlode his ancestors believed in so fervently. Varnik’s halls are lined not with treasure, but with maps, layer upon layer of meticulously charted shafts, dead ends, and dangerous collapses. His armour is dulled by dust and time, his beard singed more than once by underground gas pockets, and his face is a canvas of soot and iron-hard resolve. The younger Dwarfs see him as a relic clinging to myth, but the older Dawi respect him deeply, for he does not just seek gold, but vindication. Varnik will either strike true and restore the pride of Карак-Норн, or he will die in the dark, pick in hand.

A philosopher-lord in a hold starving for fortune, Kazrik Grimtone is as much scholar as warrior. He is the Keeper of the Stone Choir, a subterranean chamber of old oathstones, rune-inscribed memorials, and ancestral records preserved from fallen holds like Mount Silverspear. Though not a Runelord himself, he guards the histories with fierce pride and is one of the few who can recite ancient lineages from memory. Kazrik rarely takes the field unless provoked, but when he does, it is with a grim fury born of duty to memory and blood. His axe was forged from the smelted remnants of his ancestral hearth and hums with a deep, echoing resonance when swung. Dour and severe, Kazrik resents the Wood Elves most of all, not for war, but for their perceived arrogance, their indifference to the past. He dreams not of conquest or gold, but of a time when the Dwarfs of the Grey Mountains are no longer seen as relics clinging to stories, but as a people once more feared and respected.

Though Карак-Норн is now his home, Dengeir Flintmantle was born in exile, beneath the shattered remnants of Mount Silverspear. He was just a beardling when the hold fell to the onslaught of Greenskins, yet the memory of fire and stone, of screaming kin and shattered oaths, burns within him like a forge with no rest. Now one of Карак-Норн’s senior lords, Dengeir has sworn that the legacy of Silverspear shall not fade into dust. A master tactician and field commander, Dengeir leads an elite formation of warriors descended from Mount Silverspear. Their armor bears soot-markings to remind them of their ruined home, and their axes are tempered with bitter memories. Dengeir himself wears a heavy steel mantle, scorched and fused with volcanic glass, taken from the heartforge of Silverspear during its last days. He is known for his cutting insight and his scathing words, even among his own kin, but in battle he is a roaring firestorm of wrath and discipline. While others search the Grey Mountains for riches, Dengeir searches for vengeance.

Lord Dori Yngvarsson commands the southern sentry halls of Мандыдзье Pass, one of the most heavily fortified gateways in the Grey Mountains. A veteran of countless skirmishes and tense stand-offs with Bretonnian knights and wandering warbands, Dori is the embodiment of Dwarfen vigilance. Shorter than most, and built more like a stone block than a warrior, he is slow to speak and slower still to trust. He maintains the walls and bolt thrower nests of the pass with obsessive care, and while others in Карак-Норн grumble about dwindling prospects, Dori prepares. “Peace is but the whetstone of war,” he says, often to his weary engineers. With a small but elite garrison, he oversees the southern reaches of Карак-Норн’s domain and is often the first to raise the alarm of approaching trouble. Though little known outside the hold, his name is spoken with quiet reverence among his sentries, for few have held the line so long, and with such unflinching resolve.

In the shadowed depths of Карак-Норн lies a chamber known as the Weeping Vault, named for the slow, eternal drip of mineral-laden water from the cracked ceiling, a sound that echoes like a funeral dirge. It is here that Lord Bardek Stonesong holds watch, not over wealth or weapons, but over memory itself. For the Weeping Vault serves as the final resting place of countless Dwarfs whose bodies were never recovered, miners lost to collapse, warriors fallen in far-off battles, clans who vanished in the dark, all chasing after their ancestor’s hopes and dreams of wealth in the depths. Bardek, once a master stonemason and tomb-carver, was chosen to tend the Vault after a cave-in claimed his two brothers and dozens of his kin. In mourning, he took up the mantle not of vengeance, but of remembrance. His great mantle is fashioned from dark stone-weave, etched with runes of endurance and names of the fallen, worn over armor that bears more weight in grief than in steel. He carries no shield, only a greataxe, whose edge sings when it strikes, a haunting tone like keening granite. Though he rarely leaves the depths, Bardek’s word holds great sway in the council halls of Карак-Норн. His authority comes not from command in war, but from the respect earned through unshakable purpose and quiet wisdom. He ensures that even in the most forgotten reaches of the hold, the names of the dead are remembered and honored. To the young, he is a figure of myth, the grey sentinel beneath the mountain. To the old, he is a keeper of memory, the voice of the past reminding them why they must endure, even in a realm as barren as the Grey Mountains. For Bardek knows that in the end, stone may crumble and gold may fade, but the honor of the Dawi must never be buried.

Having taken the throne a hundred years past, Morgrim Ironforge has waged war and fought innumerous battles against the Greenskin tides pushing from the north and east, all the while holding the under-depths of Zhufbar from the vile Skaven hordes.

Descending from Master Engineer Burlock Damminsonn, Grimm Burloksson is the youngest Dwarf to ever reach the rank of Master Engineer. Although a master of his craft, many Longbeards believe he may be too rebellious to the Engineer Code, believing him to craft and construct designs deemed too ingenious even for his own good.

Having gone through many tribulations in his youth, none even more so than losing his arm to one of his best friends, Sven Haslefresian, Burlok Damminsonn has garnered enough recognition of his peers to be one of the Guildmasters of the Engineers guild. Burlok’s main goal is to steer his son, Grimm Burloksson, in the right direction, and not in the direction his best friend Sven went.

Grom Barakundi, the Gatekeeper of Zhufbar has held the main entrance of Zhufbar long before the birth of his current king, Morgrim Ironforge. He has staved off the threats of Vampire, Greenskin, and Skaven from the gates and walls of Zhufbar for many a millenia, and Grom vows to never see Zhufbar fall to these dreaded enemies.

Many a Dwarf knows the sound of Drammar Azrilbak’s fists, when in the sparring grounds, hence why Drammar has adopted the name “silver fist.” Having been alive quite long for the average Dwarf, Drammar has become a renowned fighter, and has been a Thane for King Morgrim Ironforge for 2 centuries.

Having served in the miners guild in Zhufbar, Rungni Ulfarsson has gained notoriety for his labor in the depths, which eventually lead to him leading a contingent of Ironbreakers to destroy a Skaven nest. Now Rungni leads throngs for his king in the depths and out.

Longbeard and avid Grumbler, Thazzrick Grundmane has a seat on the Council of the Engineer’s guild. Indeed, Thazzrick is one of the few in Zhufbar who want to steer the young Dawi towards tradition. While many don’t listen to him, he is still well respected as a warrior and an elder.

An up and coming Commander for the Armies of Zhufbar, Thrain Dronrifsson upholds a lot of respect among the younglings, having been an Ironbreaker in the mines and caverns, they look to him for guidance and training, and occasionally a drinking companion, so he can tell them all of his stories.

Old Grumbler Huunor, or just “The Old Grumbler” is one of the eldest Dawi currently residing in Zhufbar, so old he is a Living Ancestor for his Clan. He has been a Hammerer in service to Morgrim Ironforge, and the previous Kings, and now commands an army for his “new” liege. In fact many believe Huunor is only alive because he complains, gripes, and grumbles so much, he doesn’t have the time to die, but that is simply a tall tale told by the beardlings.

One of the few who remember the grand gromril mines of Karak Varn, Snorri, was one of the head prospectors, when it was besieged by the vile Skaven hordes. With a small band of miners, they made their way back to Zhufbar to swear vengeance against the raki who drove them from their precious minerals.

A natural born leader, and a natural born Dwarf, King Rorek Гранiтная Рука is both a formidable warrior, and a renowned “haver of Ale.” Many of King Гранiтная Рука’s council members let the “Lord of Ale” do as he wishes, so as to not forfeit their position.

The Great Feast of Карак-Зіфлін is a ceremony held once a month, and is among the finest feasts in all of Dwarfdom. The organizer is Dorindal Гранiтная Рука, cousin to the king. Dorindal is rarely seen not with the King, as he is always by his side filling his kingly mug with Ale. As such, Dorindal has the honors of leading Dawi under his banner, and accompanying him on campaigns whenever the king has need of him.

None hate the elves more in all of Карак-Зіфлін than Beleran. While on an expedition to gather wood for fermenting barrels in the outskirts of Атэль Лорэн, the expedition encountered Wood Elves protecting the trees and loosed volley after volley. Thinking the expedition depleted, and outnumbered, the poncy Elves went to capture the expedition. Beleran, hidden under his arrow stridden shield, emerged killing three elves and routing the rest, swearing vengeance to those who murdered his kin.

A young and aspiring commander for Карак-Зіфлін, Garatrik has proven himself worthy to command a throng of stout Dawi. Despite his relatively young age, Garatrik proved his worth by showing King Rorek his strategies to outmaneuvering Wutelgi, a feat many Dwarf have yet to do.

Thane of Rorek Гранiтная Рука, Drognir Gruumspit has served Rorek since he became king. A solid Dwarf and valuable ally to have in battle, Drognir has shown capabilities that many Dwarfs will never show in their lifetime. Although he is a strong friend to the King, Drognir has no need for King Rorek’s cousin, Dorindal, believing he wants the Throne for himself.

Legendary Ranger of the Grey Mountains, Snodrik has lived on the road most of his life, hunting beasts and creatures many would never dare to cross. Having amassed a hoard of Gorl for escorting caravans through the treacherous mountains, he decided to settle in Карак-Зіфлін, where King Rorek uses his intellect in planning trade routes to the empire and beyond.

Long before the reign of Rorek Гранiтная Рука, Marek the Elderpick has been mining in the pits of Карак-Зіфлін. Only recently did he uncover a vein of gold that he finally got reprieve from the mines. For uncovering this massive vein and adding to the treasure vaults, he was given the honor of becoming Thane, and leading troops into battle.

Byrnnoth, son of Enlag, has only recently become a lord and thane for King Гранiтная Рука. Most of his adult life he spent guarding the gates of Карак-Зіфлін, only recently gaining notoriety for fending off a Skaven assassin, who many believe was targeting King Гранiтная Рука.

An honoured friend and lord of King Гранiтная Рука, Gottri Logansson has been the Runelord for Карак-Зіфлін for Millenia, forging and inscribing runes on the arms and armours of venerable warriors who have proven their might and endurance to wield them into battle.

For many Dawi, the feast is a special occasion reserved for victories and the honouring of clan and lord. This is quite the opposite for Norr A Bolg. Instead Norr feasts anytime he can. Many of his company carry along meats, mushrooms, and ale for him to devour so his wrath is taken out on his enemies instead of his pantry.

Warlord of the Злосныя Сякеры and a self-appointed rival of Louen Orc-slayer. Gromodrak Hoofslasha is a feared old and cunning Orc warboss riding the magnificent leader of the Hagranyms called Hagroar. More than 300 years ago, Gromodrak was defeated and pushed back into the mountains by a humie boss called Louen, who was even granted the name ‘Orc-slayer’. Set on revenge, Gromodrak retreated into the Grey Mountains to once more muster the surrounding tribes. Unaware of the Orc-slayer’s passing, Gromodrak believes his rival is now called King Louen Leoncoeur and lives north of the Grey Mountains. Gromodrak is preparing his tribe for a real propa Waaagh! to destroy King Louen once and for all.

The mighty Bazodrak is a fierce Orc Boss keen on fighting as many knights as possible. He is often the first one to charge into enemy ranks with little regard for his own life. Although not as old or big as Gromodrak, he’s close to matching the Вайнабос’ fighting skill.

Kazorak often leads the raiding party set out by Gromodrak. Due to their fast Hagranym mounts, the Greenskins are often not spotted until it's too late for their victims. Kazorak loves to wield different choppas on every raid he leads.

Kragdut is a true Orc mountaineer. With his powerful arms and legs, he is often seen climbing the highest peaks of the Grey Mountains. With the blessing of Gork Kragdut uses his incredibly muscular body to fight the strongest knights and especially loves to fight at high altitudes.
Zoghag has no tongue, resulting in weird pitches when shouting his boss's orders. Nonetheless, he is a tough killa personally ending the tales of numerous knights.

Zurdrakka was once in love with a River Troll Hag. After a Bretonnian knight called Tristan the Troubadour put an end to this romance, Zurdrakka made an oath of revenge. Together with his Hagranym, he scouts Bretonnian lands, searching for his arch enemy and demanding Tristan’s head.

Kraggoth, blessed by Mork, is a hunter — an Arrer Boy Big Boss. Kraggoth has a keen nose and is a master scout, often finding lost travellers only to cruelly take their lives. He is often mocked for using a bow by his fellow Orcs, but Kraggoth knows a big bow is more than enough to bring a sure death to all humies.

Gollog is not often seen on the surface or the high mountain peaks. He would rather stay in the dark, deep caves of the Grey Mountains. But once Gollog leaves his cave home, trouble is sure to follow, for Gollog is the meanest and fastest Orc in da tribe. Swinging his choppa with such speed, even his boys can’t follow his movements.

Snazzlig, a Goblin Big Boss and second in command to Gromodrak, proved his ferocious skill by defeating Kragdrut and Zoghag in battle. No Orc knows where Snazzlig got his immense strength, but the boys are sure he is blessed by Gork.
Glartnibz leads a pack of wolf ridas. His bloodthirsty pack often travels together with Kraggoth, hunting down all humies foolish enough to try and cross the mountain passes.

Hugg became Вайнабос after aiding his predecessor in clearing out one of the larger tombs deep within the Mountains of the Pale Sisters. Once the fighting was done, he clubbed the old warboss to death with the arm of a dilapidated statue. Now, under Hugg’s command, the goblins toil endlessly at graverobbing and looting the ancient barrows of the region. As for Hugg and his boyz, they’ve turned their attention westward, launching ever bolder raids into the Bretonnian countryside, leaving only fire and broken bones in their wake.
Granug used to be a great fighter and adventurer, but one day he took an enormous arrow to the knee.

The aptly named shaman and spiritual leader of the Нікчэмы-Рубакі tribe, was not always the tribe’s Great Shaman. Once, he was merely an apprentice, learning the ways of fungus, fumes, and the Great Green from his predecessor. That changed the day Narlob was dared to consume an entire batch of highly potent mushrooms. Moments later, he erupted, quite literally, blasting his mentor to bits with a torrent of high-pressure, green vomit. Narlob spent the next three days in a coma, muttering the names of Gork and Mork between fits of frothing. When he finally awoke, his eyes glowed with a sickly green light, and his voice crackled with power. From that day forth, he was hailed as the tribe’s Great Shaman, a prophet of Gork (or possibly Mork), and few have dared to question his authority since.

Few have crossed the towering hulk that is Zogrosh and lived to tell the tale, even fewer have survived his fondness for punching his enemies into a red mist, to the awe and horror of allies and enemies alike.

Through dance and combat Stugon Bone Danca channels the mighty energies of the great greenskin gods Gork and Mork, or was it Mork and Gork?, to devastating effect. He cares little whether enemies, allies or goblins get caught in his potent magicks, just as long as the gods are pleased with the devastation.

Zorbak Bearthwakka originally comes from a tribe of Black Orcs. Killing great numbers of Dwarfs over the years, Zorbak was ultimately defeated by a Dwarfen Slayer. Left for death by his tribe but with Gork’s blessing Zorbak survived. Over time, he recovered and founded his tribe: the Чорныя Шонцы, living in the World’s Edge Mountains at the border of the planes of Zharr-Naggrund. When Zorkbak heard of the great Waaagh! tearing through the faraway Bretonnia, he and his tribe moved towards this mighty battle. Due to the harsh travels through the mountains, the Чорныя Шонцы tribe were weeks late. When they finally arrived, they were faced with a field full of dead Greenskins. Soon after, the knights of Bretonnia surrounded them, and they had a mighty last battle. Zorbak was gravely wounded, but once again with the blessing of Gork survived. Now living in the isolated caves of the Pale Sisters, Zorbak tries to muster forces once more to have the real final battle.
Zurhog is a mighty fighter, having seen much of the Old World and faced countless different foes. Although Zurhog lost several battles at the hands of humies, he still hates stunties above all.

Zagdug is known to be an instigator of internal fighting. In his opinion, propa fightin’ makes the boys stronger and ready for battle. Although halted by other Bosses, Zagdug keeps at it, often getting himself into the heat of battle.
Bazdrak is da Boss of a small company of boar ridas under the command of Zorbak. Bazdrak often leads the vanguard, dealing devastating blows to the enemy forces.
Zarklok is a lazy Orc but a great fighter. He has a strange habit of picking up the most brutal and nastiest-looking weapon after battle, only to use it in his next fight and swap it again.

Zakkhag is not a large Orc, but his wide build makes up for his smaller stature. It is even said that Zakkhag once wrestled a troll twice his size and came out on top. Da boys he leads often call him the champion of the Чорныя Шонцы.
Gazodrag has the foulest odour in the entire tribe. His whole body is covered in waste, even da choppas. His scent is so strong that enemies at a smelling distance often suffer extreme nausea.

Dazgut is a horrendously cruel Orc, often forcing smaller Orcs and Goblins to do harsh labour. Dazgut is an overseer of the fortifications and a scrap collector. He has a piercing gaze that inflicts great terror on the working crews, making them work harder.
Dazodra loves hunting down prey and stalking the mountains for lost travellers or Questing Knights. He is often confused for a Savage Orc for wearing mostly tribal armour and carrying a bow.
Orgul has a massive axe that no other Orc except for Zorbak can pick up; it is just too heavy. In his opinion, every one of the boys could pick it up, they just need to ‘get da fing up’.

Few Orcs can claim to love horns and spikes more than Mangla Bloodtusk, and fewer still derive his level of satisfaction when impaling enemies on those very spikes. The many sharp protrusions from his helmet lead to his ‘luv of ‘eadbuttin’ gits’ and few can stand their ground against a fearsome orc charging at you, like a rage filled bull.

Borbog's enthusiasm for bloody mutilation earned him the moniker of ‘Red Killa’, as he would roam the battlefield, tearing his foes apart and waving their limbs about in a glee-filled trance, spraying himself and others with a red, bloody mist.

Orcs are tough; they can shrug off wounds that would make most men cry out in agony. Even then, Umlodd Tuffgit is the toughest of the lot, often going out of his way to get wounded simply to prove that he is nigh unbeatable in ‘tuffness’.

Some believe Nog Gutgrowla wanted to prove an Orc could be just as fat as Grom the Paunch; others believe he is somehow related to ogres, given that he’s always hungry. Whatever the reality, his immensely fat frame only adds to the awesome power and force that he brings to battle

Some goblins whisper that Grut Da Skreetcha was cursed with ‘da voice of a bat’, as his voice is oddly high-pitched for an orc, and his penchant for howling at others makes it worse. Yet neither Gork nor Mork seem to have an issue with it, as his ear piercing screeches call forth the mighty magics of the orcs with unbound ferocity.

Killer of the Dawi-Zharr Daemon and successor to the Крывае Вока tribe. Bazglud promises much fighting and prosperity to the tribe. Building their weakened numbers to full strength, ready for a Waaagh! Bazglud is a brutal and cunning warrior for an Orc. His face is covered in red paint to remind his tribe who killed the red fire Daemon. This has become a sign of loyalty. With all the Bosses painting their faces red in respect to their chief.

Second in command and survivor of the Dawi-Zharr onslaught. Aggad Da Big is a huge Orc. Saved by Bazglud from being decapitated by the fire Daemon. Aggad now pledges his life to fight beside Bazglud. Painted in red, this hulking Orc is a true terror to face on the battlefield.
Part of Bazglud’s inner circle is Grombak, head of the hunters and Arrer Boys. His aim is terrible, but with enough boys at his side, nobody notices. He is especially good at shouting orders.
Equipped with his hefty axe, Morngor is ever-ready for battle. Few dare to challenge him, and Morngor is often used as the battle champion of the tribe.

Bestowed with the gift of magic, Bazgoth is an Orc shaman. As an advisor of the gods' will and wielder of potent magic, Bazgoth is often seen as the second in command aside from Aggad. The two often quarrel, but Bazgot mostly wins the arguments due to his greater knowledge.

Originally one of the Big Bosses of the long-forgotten Giant’s Foot tribe, Morlog suffered a defeat against Bazglud in a duel. After the battle, he submitted to his new overlord. Regarded as a coward for not fighting to the death, Morlog carries a great shame and dreams of being able to challenge Bazglud once more.
Fast and agile, this Orc has already planted his club between the foe’s shoulders before they could react. For Skororak, the Waaagh! is a pilgrimage to show true violence.

Exiled from his first tribe and a survivor of the destruction of his second tribe, Molglot is now a veteran Big ‘Un of the Крывае Вока tribe. Due to his un-orcish survival skills, Molglot has always stayed alive to fight another battle and to join another Waaagh! He now leads a regiment of weathered Arrer Boys.
Exiled by the Шыяломы tribe, Boggurk has found a new home in the Crooked-Eye tribe. And he has sworn revenge on his old tribe – Boggurk’s mighty fist will crush those weaklings.

Loud and obnoxious Thunderfoot always wants to be heard. A smaller but influential Orc leading a band of boyz, Thunderfoot is always recognisable on the battlefield due to his loud screaming, often ruining surprise attacks.
Groshnok is always seen talking to himself, or rather, talking to his other personality. While one of his personalities is quite rational and cunning, the other is wild and ferocious.
Urbad enjoys mocking his opponents, ripping out their eyes and consuming 'em on the spot.

Grubuk is one of the few Orcs who sees true value in gold, adorning his monstrous tusks with thick, crudely beaten rings of the stuff. In battle, he makes a point of singling out enemy commanders, hacking off their limbs before scraping away their “shiny metal bits.” He hammers these into a gleaming, misshapen lump of gold, punches a hole through it, and hangs it from one of his tusks, a grisly display of his victories and wealth alike.

Ruzzud has never been the same since devouring the finest roast boar he ever tasted. Ever since that fateful meal, he has been unable to stop drooling, his words rendered near-incoherent by a constant stream of foul-smelling spit. In his bouts of rage, Ruzzud’s furious bellowing drenches nearby foes, and allies, in a shower of stinking saliva. His slurred chanting and excessive slobbering have even altered his spellcasting, shortening the range of his magic but greatly increasing its explosive, unpredictable effect.

Bulgob is the self-proclaimed 'strajeetarist' of his Вайнабос, proud of his so-called brilliant mind and fond of testing his 'taktikz' against the brainless undead that shamble along the borders of Сыльванія. To Bulgob, the zombies make perfect test subjects, ideal for practising flanking manoeuvres, sneaky ambushes, or simply charging straight through them until they’re too broken to stand, let alone block a choppa to the skull (not that they could anyway). Bulgob is also known to take the occasional zombie prisoner, engaging in staring contests, seeing who can go longest without eating, and trying to decipher their language of moans and groans. Bulgob’s greatest ambition is to get in the mind of the mindless.

Horug has long since abandoned his choppa, ever since he got his hands on a troll’s femur. Around the camps, they tell the tale of how a river troll hag once sat on his favourite snotling. In a fit of rage, Horug tore the creature apart limb from limb, then used its severed leg to batter the remains into mush. He’s been wielding that same troll bone ever since, crushing skulls and splattering foes into bloody pulp with every swing.

Azzlod has inhaled so many potent fungus fumes that he’s somehow managed to attain a faint glimmer of clarity, or what passes for it among Greenskins. Unlike most of his kind, Azzlod speaks with surprising seriousness, and the other boys can even understand what he’s saying (most of the time). He often leads the tribe’s wild dances to appease Gork and Mork, barking orders at the other shamans and demanding they follow his steps to the letter, which proves difficult, as few of them know the difference between left and right, and Azzlod himself often forgets as well.

Cragga is said to have ‘da spikiest teef’ in the tribe. He can often be found rummaging through the scrap piles, searching for bits of metal to sharpen them with. Cragga is one of the few, if not the only, orcs who actually practises some form of dental hygiene, using rags and scraps of torn cloth to polish his teef.

Oglok is the reigning head-butting champion of the tribe, a title that has earned him great favour and the rank of boss among his kin. Unfortunately, years of smashing skulls, both his enemies’ and his own, have left his tiny brain rattled about in his thick skull. Even by greenskin standards, Oglok is considered dim-witted. Yet, when battle is joined, a spark of his old cunning returns, and he sets about clobbering foes into bloody heaps of meat. Once the fighting ends, however, the light in his eyes fades, and he soon returns to his usual, vacant state.

Grog is an abnormal orc who favours the bow over the traditional choppa, a strange choice among his kind. Grog reckons there’s no point in getting “stuck in” when you can drop your enemies from a distance. He fires massive, barbed arrows from his custom-scrapped bow, each shot loosed with brutal strength and surprising accuracy. Many have challenged Grog for his position, and just as many have hit the dirt before their choppas ever swung.

The Вайнабос of the Шмяротныя Зялёньнікі tribe and the warmonger of conflicts against the Dwarfs and Wood Elves, nobody is safe in the presence of Zorkar. Being a gigantic orc, Zorkor has no problems with ruling over his tribe. With the iron fist and a big grin, Zorkar rules with fear. He also personally slew more than a hundred Elves, Dwarfs and Humies.

Golmod is the owner of a massive choppa, which he uses to cut down trees, to taunt the Elves and Forest Spirits. Golmod's mob has invaded many halls of Атэль Лорэн, and to the surprise of the Elves, has survived any retaliation from the inhabitants of the forest.
Experienced in ‘humie fings dat lob roks', Zolog knows how to counter the heaviest of artillery — by throwing more Goblins at the problem while he and the boys charge head-on.
Known to his enemies by his powerful odor, Bolg is known as a stinky one bathing in dung to paralyse his enemies with the smell.
Aggressive and scrap-loving Olork is quickly bored and doesn’t shy away from questioning other Bosses. He is often the first one to challenge others to “keep up da spirit uv da boys”.
Cunning with an edge of brutality, Gurbak makes for a fine follower of Mork. Leading his less intelligent tribesmen into battle with “proppa Orc taktiks”.
Riding a huge war boar, Uggut is considered the best rida in the tribe, leading the boar boys into the fray.

Famous and hated in every Dwarfen hall of Карак-Норн, Ragdak Dwarfrippa has earned a proper stunty grudge. After killing a travelling party of stunty women. Ragdak has become a major target for hunting parties looking to settle this grudge once and for all.
Dolglut hates stunties with every inch of his body, and only lives to rip off their beardy ‘eads.

Cragskar lost a bet with the previous warboss and was forced to walk around with a pebble in his boot. He’s been a nuisance ever since. For weeks, Cragskar caused chaos wherever he went, kicking gobbos, stomping snotlings, and bullying other orcs just to vent his irritation. Normally, such antics would’ve gone unnoticed, but when he hurled a feral squig at the warboss, things got out of hand. All Cragskar remembers is ripping a stump out of the ground and caving the warboss’s skull in with it. And just like that, Cragskar became the new warboss. Now he leads his boys on constant raids against the Wood Elves, the Empire, and even the dreaded Крывавая Крэпасьць, all in a futile effort to distract himself from the maddening ache of the pebble still lodged in his boot… which he’s long since forgotten about.

Glob earned his name when he discovered that ‘big blokkas’ stop arrows better than tanned hides and thick skulls. With this revelation, Glob and his warband hacked their way through Asrai-infested woods with far fewer holes in them than normal, their crude shields catching volleys that would’ve killed a dozen others. To join his personal retinue, Glob devised a brutal initiation rite. Any aspiring orc must stand at the edge of a forest, bare naked save for a shield, and see how many Asrai arrows he can block before dropping. Those who survive earn a place among Glob’s personal lads.

Bugzzaz is a festering blight upon the woods, a stain the Asrai have yet to scrub from their sacred glades. After gorging himself on the strange tree-fungi of the forest, Bugzzaz became hopelessly addicted to their heady taste and pungent aroma. He can often be found squatting beside a bubbling cauldron, brewing vile stews from the forest’s fungi and any bloated insects foolish enough to crawl too close to his hut. The foul concoctions have warped him beyond reason, gifting him strange, unpredictable powers. His hexes twist with unnatural potency, and his laughter can curdle the air itself. Bugzzaz dreams of one day crafting a brew so powerful it will blanket the entire forest in a choking green fog, a ‘gift,’ he claims.

Notrak is a peculiar shade of green, greener than most, even by orc standards. His skin bears an odd hue that seems to shift and blend with his surroundings, especially beneath the shadowed boughs of the forest. Among the trees, Notrak becomes all but invisible to the naked eye, his natural camouflage allowing him to stalk and strike without warning. Because of this uncanny gift, Notrak has become a master of ambush. He’s known to drop from trees or burst from thickets with a bellowing roar, felling his prey before they even realise they’re under attack. the last thing they never see.

Azhuk is a towering Black Orc, encased in thick, blackened plate that bears the scars of countless battles. Where most of his kind favour a single great choppa or a choppa and shield, Azhuk finds this pointless. He hurls caution to the wind and wades into battle wielding two choppas in each hand as well as two extra choppas on his belt. On the battlefield, he is a hulking whirlwind of destruction, carving through friend and foe alike in his berserk rage. And should his blades ever dull or shatter, Azhuk simply reaches for another pair from his belt.

A Greenskin of muscle and mass, Dolruk has become accustomed to the hagbane-tipped arrows of the host from Атэль Лорэн. Due to his resilience, the Wood Elves struggle in dealing with the hulking beast, trying to resort to other tactics. However, all their options seem fruitless, for Dolruk loves fighting the Wood Elf hosts, and they never get a chance to change their strategy.
Skaldrut has a hobby of cutting down Forest Spirits, which he finds more entertaining boring humies. He plans on becoming the next Вайнабос and leading the next Waaagh! into Атэль Лорэн.
Zogolga doesn’t say much except for “Waaagh!” or “WAAAGH!”. Nevertheless, other boys seem to have no trouble understanding orders shouted by Zogolga.

Snagga Ironbita is the current Вайнабос of the Жалезныя Оркі. A towering hulk of muscle and black armour, Snagga is a truly peerless leader, and it would be most unwise to disregard him as a mindless brute. Calm and calculating (for an Orc), Snagga’s strategic raids have left the humies ruling surrounding lands truly perplexed. The boys of the Жалезнае Племя started calling Snagga the ‘Ironbita’ after he snapped ‘sum ‘umie git’ sword in two with his teef alone.

Not that long ago, Guzor challenged Snagga to a fight, hoping to overthrow the Вайнабос. Snagga won that duel but did not fail to recognise the ferocious fighting style of his rival. Guzor now serves as Snagga’s right hand, hoping to challenge the Вайнабос again in the future. The boys of the tribe learned to scatter quickly when Guzor is walking by, as he’s utterly merciless and greedy. Many promising lads met their deaths by Guzor’s choppa. One spiteful glare or an insufficient tribute in Teef or shiny stuff is all it takes to attract Guzor’s ire.

Crazag had a dream — To be da best and baddest Orc Bully to ever oversee a rock lobber. However, all rock lobbers he ever approached proceeded to promptly break down. This was usually preceded by a confused: “Guh, wuz diz metal bits???” from Crazag. Fortunately, the tenacious Orc did not give up and managed to turn his aspirations around. Now, whenever he marches into battle, Crazag surrounds himself with ‘trusty Goblin volunteers’ to throw and bombard the enemy with. Unsurprisingly, most Goblins prefer to take their chances as living missiles rather than serve as a potential snack.

There is only one thing Rugud adores more than a good scrap: war boars. He loves feeding ‘em, riding ‘em, petting ‘em, chopping ‘em, and eating ‘em. For Rugud, there is no sweeter sound in the world than the squealing of a boar. While most boys tend to celebrate their victorious fights with additional fighting and quarrelling, Rugud prefers tending to his pet war boar, Pigtusk. It’s not uncommon to see him personally feed Pigtusk or even lovingly brush its hide with a smaller choppa.

There is only one thing Braggat adores more than a good scrap: dead Goblins. He loves kicking ‘em, bullying ‘em, chopping ‘em, slashing ‘em, and eating ‘em. For Braggat, there is no sweeter sound in the world than the screams of a Goblin. While most boys tend to celebrate won fights with additional fighting and quarrelling, Braggat prefers running around the war camp chasing Goblins to bully or eat. It’s not uncommon to see him wrestle a Troll for that tasty Goblin snack. In battle, Braggat is a menace not only to his enemies but also to any Goblin among his ranks.

Even among his Black Orc tribesmen, Narlok is unusual. Overly grim and serious, he firmly refuses to engage in unfair fights. A choppa to the back, uneven odds or mount advantage – Narlok rejects such notions and insists on strict one-on-one fights. He also won’t hesitate to cut down any overzealous Orc that dares interfere in these duels. This, of course, does not make Narlok too popular with the boys, but they have little choice in the matter of command. Might makes right after all.

To call Karug a dimwit would be the understatement of the century. Indeed, one might have an easier time finding a lean Halfling than looking for intelligence in Karug’s actions. Da boys suspect his condition involves local Trolls and repeated blows to the head, but nevertheless, they can appreciate such simplicity in their Bosses. Fortunately for Karug, a trusty choppa is more than enough to smash in sum ‘umie or stunty skulls.

There are two extraordinary qualities to Skargut: his martial prowess and the abhorrent odour. 5 years ago, during a raid on Bretonnian lands, Skargut was seen duelling the enemy commander – A humie noble donning shiny armour. Both combatants seemed evenly matched, but Skargut’s opponent made one fatal mistake. That is, he got too close to the Orc during a clinch and dropped dead with a single whiff of Skargut’s stink. Ever since that time, Skargut has been accompanied by a small mob of loyal Big ‘Uns intent on gobbling down the most foul-smelling foodstuffs, with the hope of gaining just a bit of their Boss’s might.

Trug is the chief shaman of the Жалезнае Племя. Whenever he isn’t busy hexing insubordinate Orcs, Trug spends most of his time staring into the camp bonfire and inhaling the fumes. This allows him to commune with Gork (or Mork) and enter a particular battle trance. Most orders shouted in this state are utterly unintelligible, but weirdly enough, the boys have little difficulty in following them and smashing the enemy.

Nabrot is a cunning yet brutally direct Black Orc. After establishing his new camp, he wasted no time launching raids upon the Bretonnian countryside. With few expecting an attack from the Irrana Mountains, the southernmost villages were left virtually undefended. Nabrot’s warband swept through the land like a green tide, toppling hovels and desecrating shrines, feasting well on stolen cattle and terrified chickens. Каркасон’s knights rode out swiftly to answer the threat, but by the time they arrived, the damage was done, and Nabrot had already vanished, laden with meat and loot.

Roglum is one of the few surviving shamans of the tribe. After a frenzied dance-off that raged for fifty-two hours, he emerged as the unquestioned spiritual leader of the Скаласкуры. Roglum’s ‘magic’, if it can be called that, lies in his wild dancing, a chaotic display of stomps, jerks, and spins that somehow disrupts enemy sorcery. When Roglum truly loses himself to the rhythm, the air around him begins to shimmer and crackle with energy. He becomes a living conduit for hostile magics, drawing them in and dispelling them without even realising it.

Spurkol is an Orc boss who has suffered one beating too many at the hands of his Black Orc cousins. One day, his temper finally snapped. In a fit of blind rage, Spurkol lunged at one of his tormentors and tore him apart, ripping open his armour, then rending flesh and guts with his bare hands. The Black Orcs don’t fear Spurkol, not really, but since that day, none have dared to lay a hand on him again.

It is not uncommon for Greenskins to dig up ‘shinies’ from the mountains. While Orcs have little practical use for gold, they mine it simply to spite the other races who value it so dearly. Brugrag possesses an unusually thick skull and is often seen headbutting rock walls, training his head and searching for treasure at the same time. Because of this peculiar talent, Brugrag has proven especially useful during sieges, where he hurls himself at gates and palisades until they collapse beneath his relentless battering, allowing boys to advance unimpeded

Urruzk once nearly choked to death on a ribcage. Since that day, he has carried a massive hammer, which he uses to pulverise his foes and grind their bones to dust, just to make sure nothing ever gets stuck in his throat again.

Zugrok is most likely the oldest Orc of the Жалезнае Племя. A veteran of numerous scraps and conflicts, he was part of the great Black Orc migration from the Plains of Zharr. However, a quarrel and a lost duel against Morglum Necksnapper led to Zugrok leaving the Шыяломы and joining forces with Snagga. His weathered and scarred face is often enough to send most enemies running back to their stone castles.

Gurnak stands taller than most Жалезныя Оркі. Clad in the distinctive black armour and wielding an enormous choppa in each hand, a battle-ready Gurnak transforms into a black whirlwind of blood and death. Any foe foolish enough to engage Gurnak will be chopped to bloody bits.

Dimnak lives for killing Dwarfs – The only good stuntie is a dead stuntie. He is infamous for carrying out numerous raids on stuntie outposts in The Vaults and collecting stuntie skulls to proudly display these bearded trophies. But despite this bloodlust, Dimnak is a cunning foe: He realizes Dwarfs are tough gits, and their armor vastly outperforms most scrap the boys can cobble together. That is why Dimnak is usually seen sharpening his choppa and practising the most efficient tactics of slaying stunties in one blow.

Skulgul Horsesmakka is the current boss of the Буйныя Чопы. Skulgul came to be the leader by accidentally killing the former boss. After a bloody skirmish, the former chieftain put on a dead horse’s head, declaring himself the Horsechoppa. Skulgul, who was stunned by a recent hit, picked up his massive choppa and hacked at the horse head, killing the boss in one blow. Confused as to what happened, Skulgul cheered nonetheless and was made chieftain.

Mordrog, Skulgul’s second in command and the tribes spiritual leader. He is known amongst his tribe for killing Bretonnian humies with stomps and kicks summoned from his bare hands. Mordrog is a devout follower of Gork for violence is the solution to everything.

Ugok loves fighting horses. Many boys think that horses are weak, but after experiencing a hoof to the face, Ugok knows the opposite to be true. He loves to challenge them and smash ‘em to the ground, only to taste their flesh afterwards.

Third in command is Zakkbad, who is a cunning and merciless fighter. In battle, he enjoys riding in the vanguard and coldly staring at the enemy. Unlike other boys, Zakkbad is usually calm and doesn't lose his temper as fast. Zakkbad is often seen with Nibsnik in the caves, getting fed weird mixtures of shrooms at different times in the day.

Dakkogoth Horserippa loves ripping horses from under knights. Usually, Dakkogoth focuses on riders in battle, pulling the steeds from underneath their riders, resulting in fatal crashes. He challenges himself to rip apart the biggest horses. When the foes are underwhelming, he tends to rip the boars from underneath the boys as well.
Blessed by the hand of Gork, Doldrakk has unusually large arms and hands. With these huge fingers, Doldrakk can throw ‘bigga fings’ from a much larger range than regular orcs.

Due to a rare mutation, the appearance of Kraggut isn’t like the other orcs. Where most of the boys have muscular bodies, Kraggut has a belly and a big one at that, shaming even some of the ogres that sometimes pass through the area. Nonetheless, Kraggut is one of the best boar riders from his tribe, utilising his belly as a battering ram.
Stogrut is the only goblin in Буйнаоркал allowed to lead the boys into battle. Who appointed him a boss nobody knows or remembers, but as long as Stogrut brings ‘em to good fighting, they don’t care.
There is much Grimgul does not understand. What he understands very well is driving his choppa through weak bodies of horse humies, and he excels at it.
The shaman of the Буйныя Чопы Tribe and advisor to Skulgul is Nibsnik. This sneaky goblin shaman is an expert in the use of potent shroom potions, increasing the fighting ability of the boys.
Zaggork does the slashing, while his rival Zoggark does the smashing.
Zoggark does the smashing, while his rival Zaggork does the slashing.

A brutish and not very intelligent orc. Although he's not very different from the rest of the orcs in his clan. He led a roving clan of very small orcs, and upon reaching Буйнаоркал, there was no need to even fight Skulgul Horsesmakka, as they both knew Vishus would be defeated. So he joined with his boys to make his clan slightly larger.

A seemingly ordinary Orc. Blackfang wouldn't normally lead a mob of boys, but he has beaten everyone who has ever opposed him to the point where Greenskins follow Grommal just so they do not get slapped by him too.

Grukka was raised by Trolls, or was it Ogres? He doesn’t remember but it matters not, his bones surely come from both. Grukka is a shaman of the Зялёныя Крагі mob. When the boys are chanting he feels it in his bones, his arms, and legs. Usually, it ends with some big green emerging and smashing everything. Sometimes even causing Grukka to explode. But Grukka is still fine afterwards, must be thanks to his tuff bones.
